name: Fighter
description: A master of martial combat, skilled with a variety of weapons and armor.

features.name: Fighting Style
features.body: You adopt a particular style of fighting as your specialty. Choose one option (Archery, Defense, Dueling, Great Weapon Fighting, Protection, or Two-Weapon Fighting).

features.name: Second Wind
features.body: On your turn, you can use a bonus action to regain hit points equal to 1d10 + your fighter level. Once you use this feature, you must finish a short or long rest before you can use it again.

features.name: Action Surge
features.body: On your turn, you can take one additional action. Once you use this feature, you must finish a short or long rest before you can use it again. Starting at 17th level, you can use it twice before a rest, but only once on the same turn.

features.name: Martial Archetype
features.body: Choose an archetype that you strive to emulate in your combat styles and techniques (Champion, Battle Master, or Eldritch Knight). The archetype you choose grants you features at 3rd level and again at 7th, 10th, 15th, and 18th level.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.body: You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase a score above 20 using this feature. You can instead take a feat.

features.name: Extra Attack
features.body: You can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn. The number of attacks increases to three when you reach 11th level and to four at 20th level.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.body: You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase a score above 20 using this feature. You can instead take a feat.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.body: You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase a score above 20 using this feature. You can instead take a feat.

features.name: Indomitable
features.body: You can reroll a saving throw that you fail, but you must use the new roll. You can use this feature once per long rest. You gain a second use at 13th level and a third use at 17th level.

features.name: Extra Attack (2)
features.body: You can attack three times, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.body: You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase a score above 20 using this feature. You can instead take a feat.

features.name: Indomitable (two uses)
features.body: You can use Indomitable twice between long rests.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.body: You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase a score above 20 using this feature. You can instead take a feat.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.body: You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase a score above 20 using this feature. You can instead take a feat.

features.name: Action Surge (two uses)
features.body: You can use Action Surge twice before a rest, but only once on the same turn.

features.name: Indomitable (three uses)
features.body: You can use Indomitable three times between long rests.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.body: You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase a score above 20 using this feature. You can instead take a feat.

features.name: Extra Attack (3)
features.body: You can attack four times, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

features.name: Martial Versatility
features.body: Tasha's optional feature: whenever you gain a level in this class, you can replace one Fighting Style you know with another Fighting Style available to fighters. The swap is narrative for now — the L1 Fighting Style picker can be re-run via the Edit pill.

subclasses.name: Champion
subclasses.description: A Fighter who pursues raw physical perfection. Improved Critical, additional Fighting Style, and a survivor's grit at the highest tiers — mechanically simple, mechanically powerful.

features.name: Improved Critical
features.body: Your weapon attacks score a critical hit on a roll of 19 or 20.

features.name: Remarkable Athlete
features.body: Add half your proficiency bonus (round up) to any Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution check you make that doesn't already use your proficiency bonus. In addition, when you make a running long jump, the distance you can cover increases by a number of feet equal to your Strength modifier.

features.name: Additional Fighting Style
features.body: You can choose a second option from the Fighting Style feature.

features.name: Superior Critical
features.body: Your weapon attacks score a critical hit on a roll of 18-20.

features.name: Survivor
features.body: At the start of each of your turns, you regain hit points equal to 5 + your Constitution modifier if you have no more than half of your hit points left. You don't gain this benefit if you have 0 hit points.

subclasses.name: Battle Master
subclasses.description: A martial scholar — manoeuvres turn each attack into a tactical choice. Combat Superiority dice drive trip attacks, ripostes, feinting, and rallying allies. Maneuver picker is a follow-up; the feature text records the grant.

features.name: Combat Superiority
features.body: You learn three maneuvers of your choice from the manoeuvre list. You gain four superiority dice (d8s), expended when you use a manoeuvre and regained on a short or long rest. Save DC = 8 + proficiency bonus + STR or DEX modifier (your choice). You learn additional manoeuvres at fighter levels 7, 10, and 15. The mechanical manoeuvre picker is tracked under step 11's LevelChoice.manoeuvre follow-up.

features.name: Student of War
features.body: You gain proficiency with one type of artisan's tools of your choice.

features.name: Know Your Enemy
features.body: If you spend at least 1 minute observing or interacting with another creature outside combat, you can learn certain information about its capabilities compared to your own (relative STR/DEX/CON, AC, HP, total class levels).

features.name: Improved Combat Superiority
features.body: Your superiority dice turn into d10s. They later become d12s at 18th level.

features.name: Relentless
features.body: When you roll initiative and have no superiority dice remaining, you regain one superiority die.

subclasses.name: Eldritch Knight
subclasses.description: A fighter who supplements martial mastery with arcane study, learning wizard cantrips and 1st-level spells from L3. A third-caster: spell slots and the abjuration / evocation spell pool scale slower than a full caster, but Weapon Bond + War Magic make the Eldritch Knight a durable, self-reliant gish. (INT-based casting + the wizard spell-list pool aren't yet surfaced in the creation wizard's Spells step — tracked under the third-caster follow-up.)

features.name: Spellcasting
features.body: When you reach 3rd level, you augment your martial prowess with the ability to cast spells. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for these spells. You learn three cantrips of your choice from the wizard spell list, and your spellbook starts with three 1st-level spells (two from abjuration or evocation, one from any school). Spell slots follow the third-caster table.

features.name: Weapon Bond
features.body: At 3rd level, you learn a ritual that creates a magical bond between yourself and one weapon. You perform the ritual over the course of 1 hour, which can be done during a short rest. The weapon must be within your reach throughout the ritual, at the conclusion of which you touch the weapon and forge the bond. Once you have bonded a weapon to yourself, you can't be disarmed of that weapon unless you are incapacitated. If it is on the same plane of existence, you can summon that weapon as a bonus action on your turn, causing it to teleport instantly to your hand. You can have up to two bonded weapons, but can only summon one with a single bonus action. You must be within 5 feet of a bonded weapon to perform the ritual.

features.name: War Magic
features.body: Beginning at 7th level, when you use your action to cast a cantrip, you can make one weapon attack as a bonus action.

features.name: Eldritch Strike
features.body: At 10th level, you learn how to make your weapon strikes undercut a creature's resistance to your spells. When you hit a creature with a weapon attack, that creature has disadvantage on the next saving throw it makes against a spell you cast before the end of your next turn.

features.name: Arcane Charge
features.body: At 15th level, you gain the ability to teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see when you use your Action Surge. You can teleport before or after the additional action.

features.name: Improved War Magic
features.body: Starting at 18th level, when you use your action to cast a spell, you can make one weapon attack as a bonus action.

name: Wizard
description: A scholarly magic-user capable of manipulating the structures of reality.

features.name: Spellcasting
features.body: As a student of arcane magic, you have a spellbook containing spells that show the first glimmerings of your true power. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability.

features.name: Arcane Recovery
features.body: Once per day when you finish a short rest, you can choose expended spell slots to recover. The slots can have a combined level equal to or less than half your wizard level (rounded up), and none of the slots can be 6th level or higher.

features.name: Arcane Tradition
features.body: When you reach 2nd level, you choose an arcane tradition, shaping your practice of magic through one of eight schools (Abjuration, Conjuration, Divination, Enchantment, Evocation, Illusion, Necromancy, or Transmutation). Your choice grants you features at 2nd level and again at 6th, 10th, and 14th level.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.body: You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase a score above 20 using this feature. You can instead take a feat.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.body: You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase a score above 20 using this feature. You can instead take a feat.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.body: You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase a score above 20 using this feature. You can instead take a feat.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.body: You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase a score above 20 using this feature. You can instead take a feat.

features.name: Spell Mastery
features.body: Choose a 1st-level wizard spell and a 2nd-level wizard spell that are in your spellbook. You can cast those spells at their lowest level without expending a spell slot when you have them prepared. If you want to cast either spell at a higher level, you must expend a slot as normal. By spending 8 hours of study, you can exchange one or both of the spells for different spells of the same levels.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.body: You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase a score above 20 using this feature. You can instead take a feat.

features.name: Signature Spells
features.body: You gain mastery over two powerful spells and can cast them with little effort. Choose two 3rd-level wizard spells in your spellbook as your signature spells. You always have these spells prepared, they don't count against the number of spells you have prepared, and you can cast each of them once at 3rd level without expending a spell slot. You must finish a short or long rest before you can do so again. If you want to cast either spell at a higher level, you must expend a spell slot as normal.

features.name: Cantrip Formulas
features.body: Tasha's optional feature: at 3rd level you have scribed a set of arcane formulas in your spellbook that you can use to formulate a cantrip in your mind. Whenever you finish a long rest and consult those formulas, you can replace one wizard cantrip you know with another cantrip from the wizard spell list.

subclasses.name: School of Abjuration
subclasses.description: The School of Abjuration emphasizes magic that blocks, banishes, or protects. Hallmark: a regenerating Arcane Ward that soaks damage equal to twice your wizard level, refreshed every time you cast another abjuration spell.

features.name: Abjuration Savant
features.body: Beginning when you select this school at 2nd level, the gold and time you must spend to copy an abjuration spell into your spellbook is halved.

features.name: Arcane Ward
features.body: Starting at 2nd level, you can weave magic around yourself for protection. When you cast an abjuration spell of 1st level or higher, you can simultaneously use a strand of the spell's magic to create a magical ward on yourself that lasts until you finish a long rest. The ward has hit points equal to twice your wizard level + your Intelligence modifier. Whenever you take damage, the ward takes the damage instead. If this damage reduces the ward to 0 hit points, you take any remaining damage. While the ward has 0 hit points, it can't absorb damage, but its magic remains. Whenever you cast an abjuration spell of 1st level or higher, the ward regains a number of hit points equal to twice the level of the spell. Once you create the ward, you can't create it again until you finish a long rest.

features.name: Projected Ward
features.body: Starting at 6th level, when a creature that you can see within 30 feet of you takes damage, you can use your reaction to cause your Arcane Ward to absorb that damage. If this damage reduces the ward to 0 hit points, the warded creature takes any remaining damage.

features.name: Improved Abjuration
features.body: Beginning at 10th level, when you cast an abjuration spell that requires you to make an ability check as a part of casting that spell (as in counterspell and dispel magic), you add your proficiency bonus to that ability check.

features.name: Spell Resistance
features.body: Starting at 14th level, you have advantage on saving throws against spells. Furthermore, you have resistance against the damage of spells.

subclasses.name: School of Conjuration
subclasses.description: Conjurers summon creatures and objects from other planes — or pluck them out of nothing. Hallmark: Minor Conjuration lets you fabricate tools and mundane gear on demand, and Focused Conjuration makes your summons unbreakable in concentration.

features.name: Conjuration Savant
features.body: When you reach this level, the gold and time you must spend to copy a conjuration spell into your spellbook is halved.

features.name: Minor Conjuration
features.body: Starting at 2nd level, you can use your action to conjure up an inanimate object in your hand or on the ground in an unoccupied space that you can see within 10 feet of you. This object can be no larger than 3 feet on a side and weigh no more than 10 pounds, and its form must be that of a nonmagical object that you have seen. The object is visibly magical, radiating dim light out to 5 feet. The object disappears after 1 hour, when you use this feature again, or if it takes any damage.

features.name: Benign Transposition
features.body: Starting at 6th level, you can use your action to teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space that you can see. Alternatively, you can choose a space within range that is occupied by a Small or Medium creature. If that creature is willing, you both teleport, swapping places. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest or you cast a conjuration spell of 1st level or higher.

features.name: Focused Conjuration
features.body: Beginning at 10th level, while you are concentrating on a conjuration spell, your concentration can't be broken as a result of taking damage.

features.name: Durable Summons
features.body: Starting at 14th level, any creature that you summon or create with a conjuration spell has 30 temporary hit points.

subclasses.name: School of Divination
subclasses.description: Diviners glimpse the future and twist it. Hallmark: Portent — you roll d20s at dawn and use them later to replace any roll you or an enemy makes. Mid-fight, that means turning a critical hit into a miss, or a failed save into a success.

features.name: Divination Savant
features.body: When you reach this level, the gold and time you must spend to copy a divination spell into your spellbook is halved.

features.name: Portent
features.body: Starting at 2nd level, glimpses of the future begin to press in on your awareness. When you finish a long rest, roll two d20s and record the numbers rolled. You can replace any attack roll, saving throw, or ability check made by you or a creature that you can see with one of these foretelling rolls. You must choose to do so before the roll, and you can replace a roll in this way only once per turn. Each foretelling roll can be used only once. When you finish a long rest, you lose any unused foretelling rolls.

features.name: Expert Divination
features.body: Beginning at 6th level, casting divination spells comes so easily to you that it expends only a fraction of your spellcasting efforts. When you cast a divination spell of 2nd level or higher using a spell slot, you regain one expended spell slot. The slot you regain must be of a level lower than the spell you cast and can't be higher than 5th level.

features.name: The Third Eye
features.body: Starting at 10th level, you can use your action to increase your powers of perception. When you do so, choose one of the following benefits, which lasts until you are incapacitated or you take a short or long rest. You can't use the feature again until you finish a rest: Darkvision out to 60 feet; Ethereal Sight (60 ft); Greater Comprehension (read any language); See Invisibility (10 ft).

features.name: Greater Portent
features.body: Starting at 14th level, the visions in your dreams intensify and paint a more accurate picture in your mind of what is to come. You roll three d20s for your Portent feature, rather than two.

subclasses.name: School of Enchantment
subclasses.description: Enchanters bend minds — charm, command, control. Hallmark: Hypnotic Gaze freezes a single creature in place every encounter, and Instinctive Charm bounces attacks onto someone else.

features.name: Enchantment Savant
features.body: When you reach this level, the gold and time you must spend to copy an enchantment spell into your spellbook is halved.

features.name: Hypnotic Gaze
features.body: Starting at 2nd level, your soft words and enchanting gaze can magically enthrall another creature. As an action, choose one creature that you can see within 5 feet of you. If the target can see or hear you, it must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your wizard spell save DC or be charmed by you until the end of your next turn. The charmed creature's speed drops to 0, and the creature is incapacitated and visibly dazed. On subsequent turns, you can use your action to maintain this effect, extending its duration until the end of your next turn. However, the effect ends if the creature ends its turn out of line of sight or more than 60 feet away from you. Once the effect ends, or if the creature succeeds on its initial saving throw against this effect, you can't use this feature on that creature again until you finish a long rest.

features.name: Instinctive Charm
features.body: Beginning at 6th level, when a creature you can see within 30 feet of you makes an attack roll against you, you can use your reaction to divert the attack, provided that another creature is within the attack's range. The attacker must make a Wisdom saving throw against your wizard spell save DC. On a failed save, the attacker must target the creature that is closest to it, not including you or itself. If multiple creatures are closest, the attacker chooses which one to target. On a successful save, you can't use this feature on the attacker again until you finish a long rest. You must choose to use this feature before knowing whether the attack hits or misses.

features.name: Split Enchantment
features.body: Starting at 10th level, when you cast an enchantment spell of 1st level or higher that targets only one creature, it can target a second creature.

features.name: Alter Memories
features.body: At 14th level, you gain the ability to make a creature unaware of your magical influence on it. When you cast an enchantment spell to charm one or more creatures, you can alter one creature's understanding so that it remains unaware of being charmed. Additionally, once before the spell expires, you can use your action to try to make the chosen creature forget some of the time it spent charmed. The creature must succeed on an Intelligence saving throw against your wizard spell save DC or lose a number of hours of its memories equal to 1 + your Charisma modifier (minimum 1).

subclasses.name: School of Evocation
subclasses.description: Evocation wizards channel raw elemental energy into the world — fire, lightning, thunder, force. Hallmark abilities reshape their own AoE spells around allies and squeeze more damage from every cast.

features.name: Evocation Savant
features.body: When you reach this level, the gold and time you must spend to copy an evocation spell into your spellbook is halved.

features.name: Sculpt Spells
features.body: When you cast an evocation spell that affects other creatures you can see, you can choose a number of them equal to 1 + the spell's level. The chosen creatures automatically succeed on their saving throws against the spell, and they take no damage if they would normally take half damage on a successful save.

features.name: Potent Cantrip
features.body: Your damaging cantrips affect even creatures that avoid the brunt of the effect. When a creature succeeds on a saving throw against your cantrip, the creature takes half the cantrip's damage (if any) but suffers no additional effect from the cantrip.

features.name: Empowered Evocation
features.body: You can add your Intelligence modifier to one damage roll of any wizard evocation spell you cast.

features.name: Overchannel
features.body: When you cast a wizard spell of 1st through 5th level that deals damage, you can deal maximum damage with that spell. The first time you do so, you suffer no adverse effect. If you use this feature again before you finish a long rest, you take 2d12 necrotic damage for each level of the spell, immediately after you cast it. Each time you use this feature again before finishing a long rest, the necrotic damage per spell level increases by 1d12. This damage ignores resistance and immunity.

subclasses.name: School of Illusion
subclasses.description: Illusionists deceive senses and bend perception. Hallmark: Malleable Illusions lets you reshape an active illusion mid-cast, and at L14 you can turn parts of an illusion into actual reality.

features.name: Illusion Savant
features.body: When you reach this level, the gold and time you must spend to copy an illusion spell into your spellbook is halved.

features.name: Improved Minor Illusion
features.body: When you choose this school at 2nd level, you learn the minor illusion cantrip. If you already know it, you learn a different wizard cantrip of your choice. The cantrip doesn't count against your number of cantrips known. When you cast minor illusion, you can create both a sound and an image with a single casting of the spell.

features.name: Malleable Illusions
features.body: Starting at 6th level, when you cast an illusion spell that has a duration of 1 minute or longer, you can use your action to change the nature of that illusion (using the spell's normal parameters for the illusion), provided that you can see the illusion.

features.name: Illusory Self
features.body: Beginning at 10th level, you can create an illusory duplicate of yourself as an instant, almost instinctual reaction to danger. When a creature makes an attack roll against you, you can use your reaction to interpose the illusory duplicate between the attacker and yourself. The attack automatically misses you, then the illusion dissipates. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

features.name: Illusory Reality
features.body: By 14th level, you have learned the secret of weaving shadow magic into your illusions to give them a semi-reality. When you cast an illusion spell of 1st level or higher, you can choose one inanimate, nonmagical object that is part of the illusion and make that object real. You can do this on your turn as a bonus action while the spell is ongoing. The object remains real for 1 minute.

subclasses.name: School of Necromancy
subclasses.description: Necromancers manipulate the energies of life, death, and undeath. Hallmark: Grim Harvest heals you off every killing-blow spell, and Undead Thralls turns Animate Dead into a much beefier army with each cast.

features.name: Necromancy Savant
features.body: When you reach this level, the gold and time you must spend to copy a necromancy spell into your spellbook is halved.

features.name: Grim Harvest
features.body: At 2nd level, you gain the ability to reap life energy from creatures you kill with your spells. Once per turn when you kill one or more creatures with a spell of 1st level or higher, you regain hit points equal to twice the spell's level, or three times its level if the spell belongs to the School of Necromancy. You don't gain this benefit for killing constructs or undead.

features.name: Undead Thralls
features.body: At 6th level, you add the animate dead spell to your spellbook if it is not there already. When you cast animate dead, you can target one additional corpse or pile of bones, creating another zombie or skeleton, as appropriate. Whenever you create an undead using a necromancy spell, it has additional benefits: the creature's hit point maximum is increased by an amount equal to your wizard level; the creature adds your proficiency bonus to its weapon damage rolls.

features.name: Inured to Undeath
features.body: Beginning at 10th level, you have resistance to necrotic damage, and your hit point maximum can't be reduced. You have spent so much time dealing with undead and the forces that animate them that you have become inured to some of their worst effects.

features.name: Command Undead
features.body: Starting at 14th level, you can use magic to bring undead under your control, even those created by other wizards. As an action, you can choose one undead that you can see within 60 feet of you. That creature must make a Charisma saving throw against your wizard spell save DC. On a failed save, the creature falls under your control for 24 hours, obeying your commands and not attacking you. Intelligent undead get advantage on the save; an INT 8+ undead can repeat the save every hour, and INT 12+ does so every minute. If the save succeeds, you can't use this feature on that creature again.

subclasses.name: School of Transmutation
subclasses.description: Transmuters reshape matter and energy — turning lead into gold, transforming people into beasts, granting magical enhancements to allies. Hallmark: the Transmuter's Stone, a swappable attunement that grants darkvision / speed / save proficiency / resistance.

features.name: Transmutation Savant
features.body: When you reach this level, the gold and time you must spend to copy a transmutation spell into your spellbook is halved.

features.name: Minor Alchemy
features.body: Starting at 2nd level, you can temporarily alter the physical properties of one nonmagical object, changing it from one substance into another. You perform a special alchemical procedure on one object composed entirely of wood, stone (but not a gemstone), iron, copper, or silver, transforming it into a different one of those materials. For each 10 minutes you spend performing the procedure, you can transform up to 1 cubic foot of material. After 1 hour, or until you lose your concentration (as if you were concentrating on a spell), the material reverts to its original substance.

features.name: Transmuter's Stone
features.body: Starting at 6th level, you can spend 8 hours creating a transmuter's stone that stores transmutation magic. You can benefit from the stone yourself or give it to another creature. A creature gains a benefit of your choice as long as the stone is in the creature's possession: darkvision out to 60 feet; an increase to speed of 10 feet while the creature is unencumbered; proficiency in Constitution saving throws; or resistance to acid, cold, fire, lightning, or thunder damage (your choice when the stone is created). Each time you cast a transmutation spell of 1st level or higher, you can change the effect of your stone if it is on your person.

features.name: Shapechanger
features.body: At 10th level, you add the polymorph spell to your spellbook, if it is not there already. You can cast polymorph without expending a spell slot. When you do so, you can target only yourself and transform into a beast whose challenge rating is 1 or lower. Once you cast polymorph in this way, you can't do so again until you finish a short or long rest, though you can still cast it normally using an available spell slot.

features.name: Master Transmuter
features.body: Starting at 14th level, you can use your action to consume the reserve of transmutation magic stored within your transmuter's stone in a single burst. When you do so, choose one of the following effects: Major Transformation (transform one non-magical object up to 5 ft on a side into another object of similar size and mass and equal or lesser value); Panacea (remove curses, diseases, poisons; restore HP); Restore Life (cast raise dead as an action, no material); Restore Youth (target's apparent age reduced by 3d10 years, minimum 13). Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

subclasses.name: Bladesinging
subclasses.description: Bladesingers are elven wizard-warriors who weave spell and sword into a dance of grace and lethality. The classic 5e gish — entering Bladesong gives a Wizard the front-line stats they always wished they had: AC bonus, speed boost, concentration advantage, and an extra attack at L6.

features.name: Training in War and Song
features.body: When you adopt this tradition at 2nd level, you gain proficiency with light armor, and you gain proficiency with one type of one-handed melee weapon of your choice. You also gain proficiency in the Performance skill if you don't already have it.

features.name: Bladesong
features.body: Starting at 2nd level, you can invoke an elven magic called the Bladesong, provided that you aren't wearing medium or heavy armor or using a shield. As a bonus action, you can begin the Bladesong, which lasts for 1 minute. It ends early if you are incapacitated, if you don the disallowed armor or pick up a shield, or if you use two hands to make an attack with a weapon. While your Bladesong is active, you gain the following benefits: a bonus to AC equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum +1); your walking speed increases by 10 feet; you have advantage on Dexterity (Acrobatics) checks; and you gain a bonus to any Constitution saving throw you make to maintain your concentration on a spell, equal to your Intelligence modifier. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a short or long rest.

features.name: Extra Attack
features.body: Starting at 6th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn. Moreover, you can cast one of your cantrips in place of one of those attacks.

features.name: Song of Defense
features.body: Beginning at 10th level, you can direct your magic to absorb damage while your Bladesong is active. When you take damage, you can use your reaction to expend one spell slot and reduce that damage to you by an amount equal to five times the slot's level.

features.name: Song of Victory
features.body: Starting at 14th level, you add your Intelligence modifier (minimum of +1) to the damage of your melee weapon attacks while your Bladesong is active.

name: Cleric
description: A priestly champion who wields divine magic in service of a higher power.

features.name: Spellcasting
features.body: As a conduit for divine power, you can cast cleric spells. Wisdom is your spellcasting ability.

features.name: Divine Domain
features.body: Choose one domain related to your deity (Knowledge, Life, Light, Nature, Tempest, Trickery, or War). Your choice grants you domain spells and other features when you choose it at 1st level.

features.name: Channel Divinity
features.body: You can channel divine energy directly from your deity, using that energy to fuel magical effects. You start with two such effects: Turn Undead and an effect determined by your domain. Each use, you choose which effect to create. You must finish a short or long rest to use the feature again. Save DCs equal your cleric spell save DC. Uses scale to 2/rest at 6th level and 3/rest at 18th level.

features.name: Turn Undead
features.body: As an action, you present your holy symbol and speak a prayer censuring the undead. Each undead that can see or hear you within 30 feet must make a Wisdom saving throw. If it fails, it is turned for 1 minute or until it takes any damage. A turned creature must spend its turns trying to move as far from you as it can, can't willingly move to a space within 30 feet of you, can't take reactions, and can use only the Dash action or try to escape an effect that prevents it from moving.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.body: You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase a score above 20 using this feature. You can instead take a feat.

features.name: Destroy Undead (CR 1/2)
features.body: When an undead fails its saving throw against your Turn Undead feature, the creature is instantly destroyed if its challenge rating is 1/2 or lower.

features.name: Channel Divinity (2/rest)
features.body: You can use your Channel Divinity twice between rests.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.body: You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase a score above 20 using this feature. You can instead take a feat.

features.name: Destroy Undead (CR 1)
features.body: Undead destroyed by your Turn Undead feature now includes creatures of challenge rating 1 or lower.

features.name: Divine Intervention
features.body: You can call on your deity to intervene on your behalf when your need is great. As an action, describe the assistance you seek and roll percentile dice. If you roll a number equal to or lower than your cleric level, your deity intervenes (the GM chooses the nature of the intervention). On success, you can't use this feature again for 7 days; otherwise you can use it again after a long rest. At 20th level, your call succeeds automatically.

features.name: Destroy Undead (CR 2)
features.body: Undead destroyed by your Turn Undead feature now includes creatures of challenge rating 2 or lower.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.body: You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase a score above 20 using this feature. You can instead take a feat.

features.name: Destroy Undead (CR 3)
features.body: Undead destroyed by your Turn Undead feature now includes creatures of challenge rating 3 or lower.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.body: You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase a score above 20 using this feature. You can instead take a feat.

features.name: Destroy Undead (CR 4)
features.body: Undead destroyed by your Turn Undead feature now includes creatures of challenge rating 4 or lower.

features.name: Channel Divinity (3/rest)
features.body: You can use your Channel Divinity three times between rests.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.body: You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase a score above 20 using this feature. You can instead take a feat.

features.name: Divine Intervention Improvement
features.body: Your call for intervention succeeds automatically, no roll required.

features.name: Channel Divinity (L1)
features.body: Tasha's alternative: Channel Divinity comes online at 1st level instead of 2nd. Mechanics are otherwise identical to the standard Channel Divinity feature. Hides the PHB L2 Channel Divinity grant when active.

features.name: Cantrip Versatility
features.body: Tasha's optional feature: whenever you finish a long rest, you can replace one cantrip you learned from this class's spellcasting feature with a different cantrip from the cleric spell list.

subclasses.name: Knowledge Domain
subclasses.description: Gods of knowledge value learning and understanding above all. Their clerics serve as sages and scholars, voracious for any fragment of insight into the workings of the world. Hallmark: pick up new tools and skills on demand via Channel Divinity, plus Potent Spellcasting for cantrip-heavy builds.

features.name: Blessings of Knowledge
features.body: At 1st level, you learn two languages of your choice. You also become proficient in your choice of two of the following skills: Arcana, History, Nature, or Religion. Your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check you make that uses either of those skills.

features.name: Channel Divinity: Knowledge of the Ages
features.body: Starting at 2nd level, you can use your Channel Divinity to tap into a divine well of knowledge. As an action, you choose one skill or tool. For 10 minutes, you have proficiency with the chosen skill or tool.

features.name: Channel Divinity: Read Thoughts
features.body: At 6th level, you can use your Channel Divinity to read a creature's thoughts. As an action, choose one creature you can see within 60 feet of you. That creature must make a Wisdom saving throw. If the creature succeeds, you can't use this feature on it again until you finish a long rest. If fails, you can read its surface thoughts for 1 minute as long as it stays within 60 feet of you. As an action you can end this and cast suggestion on the creature without expending a spell slot — automatically failing the save.

features.name: Potent Spellcasting
features.body: Starting at 8th level, you add your Wisdom modifier to the damage you deal with any cleric cantrip.

features.name: Visions of the Past
features.body: Starting at 17th level, you can call up visions of the past that relate to an object you hold or your immediate surroundings. You spend at least 1 minute in meditation and prayer, then receive dreamlike, shadowy glimpses of recent events. Object reading reveals events of the past day per minute (max 7 days); area reading reveals events within 50 feet of the past 24 hours per minute (max 7 days). Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

subclasses.name: Life Domain
subclasses.description: The Life Domain focuses on the vibrant positive energy that sustains all life. Healing the sick and dying is the bread and butter of a Life cleric — they squeeze every drop of HP out of every cure they cast.

features.name: Bonus Proficiency
features.body: When you choose this domain at 1st level, you gain proficiency with heavy armor.

features.name: Disciple of Life
features.body: Whenever you use a 1st-level or higher spell to restore hit points to a creature, the creature regains additional hit points equal to 2 + the spell's level.

features.name: Channel Divinity: Preserve Life
features.body: As an action, you present your holy symbol and evoke healing energy. Choose any creatures within 30 feet of you and divide hit points equal to five times your cleric level among them. This feature can restore a creature to no more than half of its hit point maximum. You can't use this feature on an undead or a construct.

features.name: Blessed Healer
features.body: The healing spells you cast on others heal you as well: when you cast a spell of 1st level or higher that restores hit points to a creature other than you, you regain hit points equal to 2 + the spell's level.

features.name: Divine Strike
features.body: Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can cause the attack to deal an extra 1d8 radiant damage to the target. When you reach 14th level, the extra damage increases to 2d8.

features.name: Supreme Healing
features.body: When you would normally roll one or more dice to restore hit points with a spell, you instead use the highest number possible for each die. (For example, instead of restoring 2d6 hit points to a creature, you restore 12.)

subclasses.name: Light Domain
subclasses.description: Gods of light promote ideals of rebirth and renewal, truth, vigilance, and beauty. Clerics raise the sun, manifest pure light, and burn enemies with sacred radiance. Hallmark: Warding Flare lets you reaction-impose disadvantage on attackers, and at high levels you turn into a literal lantern of doom.

features.name: Bonus Cantrip
features.body: When you choose this domain at 1st level, you gain the light cantrip if you don't already know it.

features.name: Warding Flare
features.body: Also at 1st level, you can interpose divine light between yourself and an attacking enemy. When you are attacked by a creature within 30 feet of you that you can see, you can use your reaction to impose disadvantage on the attack roll, causing light to flare before the attacker before it hits or misses. An attacker that can't be blinded is immune to this feature. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (a minimum of once). You regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

features.name: Channel Divinity: Radiance of the Dawn
features.body: Starting at 2nd level, you can use your Channel Divinity to harness sunlight, banishing darkness and dealing radiant damage. As an action, you present your holy symbol, and any magical darkness within 30 feet of you is dispelled. Additionally, each hostile creature within 30 feet of you must make a Constitution saving throw. A creature takes radiant damage equal to 2d10 + your cleric level on a failed save, and half as much damage on a successful one.

features.name: Improved Flare
features.body: Starting at 6th level, you can also use your Warding Flare feature when a creature that you can see within 30 feet of you attacks a creature other than you.

features.name: Potent Spellcasting
features.body: Starting at 8th level, you add your Wisdom modifier to the damage you deal with any cleric cantrip.

features.name: Corona of Light
features.body: Starting at 17th level, you can use your action to activate an aura of sunlight that lasts for 1 minute or until you dismiss it using another action. You emit bright light in a 60-foot radius and dim light 30 feet beyond that. Your enemies in the bright light have disadvantage on saving throws against any spell that deals fire or radiant damage.

subclasses.name: Nature Domain
subclasses.description: Gods of nature are as varied as the natural world itself, from inscrutable gods of the deep forests to friendly deities of streams and meadows. Druidic clerics — straddling the line between two traditions. Hallmark: nature-themed cantrip + heavy armor + a sphere-of-influence over plants and beasts.

features.name: Acolyte of Nature
features.body: At 1st level, you learn one druid cantrip of your choice. You also gain proficiency in one of the following skills of your choice: Animal Handling, Nature, or Survival.

features.name: Bonus Proficiency
features.body: Also at 1st level, you gain proficiency with heavy armor.

features.name: Channel Divinity: Charm Animals and Plants
features.body: Starting at 2nd level, you can use your Channel Divinity to charm animals and plants. As an action, you present your holy symbol and invoke the name of your deity. Each beast or plant creature that can see you within 30 feet of you must make a Wisdom saving throw. If the creature fails its saving throw, it is charmed by you for 1 minute or until it takes damage. While charmed, it is friendly to you and other creatures you designate.

features.name: Dampen Elements
features.body: Starting at 6th level, when you or a creature within 30 feet of you takes acid, cold, fire, lightning, or thunder damage, you can use your reaction to grant resistance to the creature against that instance of the damage.

features.name: Divine Strike
features.body: At 8th level, you gain the ability to infuse your weapon strikes with divine energy. Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can cause the attack to deal an extra 1d8 cold, fire, or lightning damage to the target (your choice). When you reach 14th level, the extra damage increases to 2d8.

features.name: Master of Nature
features.body: At 17th level, you gain the ability to command animals and plant creatures. While creatures are charmed by your Charm Animals and Plants feature, you can take a bonus action on your turn to verbally command what each of those creatures will do on its next turn.

subclasses.name: Tempest Domain
subclasses.description: Gods whose portfolios include the Tempest domain — among them Talos, Umberlee, Kord, Zeboim, Thor — govern storms, sea, and sky. Their clerics are the chosen of thunder gods, hurling lightning and storm. Hallmark: max-damage thunder/lightning crits via Destructive Wrath + a reaction zap whenever something hits you.

features.name: Bonus Proficiencies
features.body: At 1st level, you gain proficiency with martial weapons and heavy armor.

features.name: Wrath of the Storm
features.body: Also at 1st level, you can thunderously rebuke attackers. When a creature within 5 feet of you that you can see hits you with an attack, you can use your reaction to deal 2d8 lightning or thunder damage (your choice) to that creature. The creature must make a Dexterity saving throw — on a successful save, the creature takes half damage. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (a minimum of once). You regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

features.name: Channel Divinity: Destructive Wrath
features.body: Starting at 2nd level, you can use your Channel Divinity to wield the power of the storm with unchecked ferocity. When you roll lightning or thunder damage, you can use your Channel Divinity to deal maximum damage, instead of rolling.

features.name: Thunderbolt Strike
features.body: At 6th level, when you deal lightning damage to a Large or smaller creature, you can also push it up to 10 feet away from you.

features.name: Divine Strike
features.body: At 8th level, you gain the ability to infuse your weapon strikes with divine energy. Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can cause the attack to deal an extra 1d8 thunder damage to the target. When you reach 14th level, the extra damage increases to 2d8.

features.name: Stormborn
features.body: At 17th level, you have a flying speed equal to your current walking speed whenever you are not underground or indoors.

subclasses.name: Trickery Domain
subclasses.description: Gods of trickery — such as Tymora, Beshaba, Olidammara, the Traveler, Garl Glittergold, and Loki — are mischief-makers and instigators who stand as a constant challenge to the accepted order. Hallmark: illusion-fueled Invoke Duplicity gives you an attack-advantage projection, and at L17 you have four of them at once.

features.name: Blessing of the Trickster
features.body: Starting when you choose this domain at 1st level, you can use your action to touch a willing creature other than yourself to give it advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks. This blessing lasts for 1 hour or until you use this feature again.

features.name: Channel Divinity: Invoke Duplicity
features.body: Starting at 2nd level, you can use your Channel Divinity to create an illusory duplicate of yourself. As an action, you create a perfect illusion of yourself that lasts for 1 minute, or until you lose your concentration. The illusion appears in an unoccupied space that you can see within 30 feet of you. As a bonus action on your turn, you can move the illusion up to 30 feet to a space you can see, but it must remain within 120 feet of you. While the illusion persists, you can cast spells as though you were in the illusion's space, but you must use your own senses. Additionally, when both you and your illusion are within 5 feet of a creature that can see the illusion, you have advantage on attack rolls against that creature, given how distracting the illusion is to the target.

features.name: Channel Divinity: Cloak of Shadows
features.body: Starting at 6th level, you can use your Channel Divinity to vanish. As an action, you become invisible until the end of your next turn. You become visible if you attack or cast a spell.

features.name: Divine Strike
features.body: At 8th level, you gain the ability to infuse your weapon strikes with poison — a gift from your deity. Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can cause the attack to deal an extra 1d8 poison damage to the target. When you reach 14th level, the extra damage increases to 2d8.

features.name: Improved Duplicity
features.body: At 17th level, you can create up to four duplicates of yourself, instead of one, when you use Invoke Duplicity. As a bonus action on your turn, you can move any number of them up to 30 feet, to a maximum range of 120 feet.

subclasses.name: War Domain
subclasses.description: War has many manifestations. It can make heroes of ordinary people. Cleric of War lean into front-line combat — bonus action attacks, +10 to attack rolls or AC via Channel Divinity, eventually magic strikes on every swing.

features.name: Bonus Proficiencies
features.body: At 1st level, you gain proficiency with martial weapons and heavy armor.

features.name: War Priest
features.body: From 1st level, your god delivers bolts of inspiration to you while you are engaged in battle. When you use the Attack action, you can make one weapon attack as a bonus action. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (a minimum of once). You regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

features.name: Channel Divinity: Guided Strike
features.body: Starting at 2nd level, you can use your Channel Divinity to strike with supernatural accuracy. When you make an attack roll, you can use your Channel Divinity to gain a +10 bonus to the roll. You make this choice after you see the roll, but before the DM says whether the attack hits or misses.

features.name: Channel Divinity: War God's Blessing
features.body: At 6th level, when a creature within 30 feet of you makes an attack roll, you can use your reaction to grant that creature a +10 bonus to the roll, using your Channel Divinity. You make this choice after you see the roll, but before the DM says whether the attack hits or misses.

features.name: Divine Strike
features.body: At 8th level, once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can cause the attack to deal an extra 1d8 damage of the same type dealt by the weapon. When you reach 14th level, the extra damage increases to 2d8.

features.name: Avatar of Battle
features.body: At 17th level, you gain resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks.

subclasses.name: Twilight Domain
subclasses.description: The Twilight Domain serves gods who deliver mortals' souls safely from the night, who illuminate the world at dusk and dawn, and who watch over the boundary between life and death. Hallmark: a 30-foot Twilight Sanctuary aura that gives every ally either temp HP or charm-/fear-removal each round.

features.name: Bonus Proficiencies
features.body: When you choose this domain at 1st level, you gain proficiency with martial weapons and heavy armor.

features.name: Eyes of Night
features.body: Starting at 1st level, you can see through deepest gloom. You have darkvision out to a range of 300 feet. As an action, you can magically share the darkvision of this trait with willing creatures you can see within 10 feet of you, up to a number of creatures equal to your Wisdom modifier (a minimum of one). The shared darkvision lasts for 1 hour. Once you share it, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest, unless you expend a spell slot of any level to share it again.

features.name: Vigilant Blessing
features.body: At 1st level, the night has taught you to be vigilant. As an action, you give one creature you touch (including possibly yourself) advantage on the next initiative roll the creature makes. This benefit ends immediately after the roll or if you use this feature again.

features.name: Channel Divinity: Twilight Sanctuary
features.body: Starting at 2nd level, you can use your Channel Divinity to refresh your allies with soothing twilight. As an action, you present your holy symbol, and a sphere of twilight emanates from you. The sphere is centered on you, has a 30-foot radius, and is filled with dim light. The sphere moves with you, and it lasts for 1 minute or until you are incapacitated or die. Whenever a creature (including you) ends its turn in the sphere, you can grant that creature one of these benefits: you give it temporary hit points equal to 1d6 plus your cleric level; or you end one effect on it causing it to be charmed or frightened.

features.name: Steps of Night
features.body: Starting at 6th level, you can draw on the mystical power of night to rise into the air. As a bonus action when you are in dim light or darkness, you can magically give yourself a flying speed equal to your walking speed for 1 minute. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

features.name: Divine Strike
features.body: At 8th level, you gain the ability to infuse your weapon strikes with divine energy. Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can cause the attack to deal an extra 1d8 radiant damage to the target. When you reach 14th level, the extra damage increases to 2d8.

features.name: Twilight Shroud
features.body: At 17th level, the twilight that you summon offers a protective embrace: you and your allies have half cover while in the sphere created by your Twilight Sanctuary.

name: Rogue
description: A scoundrel who uses stealth and trickery to overcome obstacles and enemies.

features.name: Expertise
features.body: Choose two of your skill proficiencies, or one of your skill proficiencies and your proficiency with thieves' tools. Your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check you make that uses either of the chosen proficiencies.

features.name: Sneak Attack
features.body: Once per turn, you can deal an extra 1d6 damage to one creature you hit with an attack if you have advantage on the attack roll. The attack must use a finesse or ranged weapon. You don't need advantage if another enemy of the target is within 5 feet of it and you don't have disadvantage. Damage increases by 1d6 at every odd rogue level (3rd, 5th, 7th, ..., 19th).

features.name: Thieves' Cant
features.body: You have learnt thieves' cant, a secret mix of dialect, jargon, and code that lets you hide messages in seemingly normal conversation.

features.name: Cunning Action
features.body: Your quick thinking and agility allow you to move and act quickly. You can take a bonus action on each of your turns in combat. The action can be used only to take the Dash, Disengage, or Hide action.

features.name: Roguish Archetype
features.body: Choose an archetype that you emulate in the exercise of your rogue abilities (Thief, Assassin, or Arcane Trickster). Your archetype grants you features at 3rd level and again at 9th, 13th, and 17th level.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.body: You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase a score above 20 using this feature. You can instead take a feat.

features.name: Uncanny Dodge
features.body: When an attacker that you can see hits you with an attack, you can use your reaction to halve the attack's damage against you.

features.name: Expertise (additional)
features.body: Choose two more of your proficiencies (in skills or with thieves' tools) to gain expertise — your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check you make that uses either of the chosen proficiencies.

features.name: Evasion
features.body: You can nimbly dodge out of the way of certain area effects. When you are subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw, and only half damage if you fail.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.body: You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase a score above 20 using this feature. You can instead take a feat.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.body: You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase a score above 20 using this feature. You can instead take a feat.

features.name: Reliable Talent
features.body: You have refined your chosen skills until they approach perfection. Whenever you make an ability check that lets you add your proficiency bonus, you can treat a d20 roll of 9 or lower as a 10.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.body: You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase a score above 20 using this feature. You can instead take a feat.

features.name: Blindsense
features.body: If you are able to hear, you are aware of the location of any hidden or invisible creature within 10 feet of you.

features.name: Slippery Mind
features.body: You have acquired greater mental strength. You gain proficiency in Wisdom saving throws.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.body: You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase a score above 20 using this feature. You can instead take a feat.

features.name: Elusive
features.body: You are so evasive that attackers rarely gain the upper hand against you. No attack roll has advantage against you while you aren't incapacitated.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.body: You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase a score above 20 using this feature. You can instead take a feat.

features.name: Stroke of Luck
features.body: You have an uncanny knack for succeeding when you need to. If your attack misses a target within range, you can turn the miss into a hit. Alternatively, if you fail an ability check, you can treat the d20 roll as a 20. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

features.name: Steady Aim
features.body: Tasha's optional feature: as a bonus action, you give yourself advantage on your next attack roll on the current turn. You can use this bonus action only if you haven't moved during this turn, and after you use the bonus action, your speed is 0 until the end of the current turn.

subclasses.name: Thief
subclasses.description: Quick-fingered larcenist who uses speed and dexterity to outpace any obstacle. Burglars, treasure hunters, and the occasional adventurer-spy lean on these tools. Hallmarks: bonus-action utility, urban traversal, and the only PHB rogue who gets a second turn in round one.

features.name: Fast Hands
features.body: You can use the bonus action granted by your Cunning Action to make a Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check, use your thieves' tools to disarm a trap or open a lock, or take the Use an Object action.

features.name: Second-Story Work
features.body: When you choose this archetype at 3rd level, you gain the ability to climb faster than normal; climbing no longer costs you extra movement. In addition, when you make a running jump, the distance you cover increases by a number of feet equal to your Dexterity modifier.

features.name: Supreme Sneak
features.body: Starting at 9th level, you have advantage on a Dexterity (Stealth) check if you move no more than half your speed on the same turn.

features.name: Use Magic Device
features.body: By 13th level, you have learned enough about the workings of magic that you can improvise the use of items even when they are not intended for you. You ignore all class, race, and level requirements on the use of magic items.

features.name: Thief's Reflexes
features.body: When you reach 17th level, you have become adept at laying ambushes and quickly escaping danger. You can take two turns during the first round of any combat. You take your first turn at your normal initiative and your second turn at your initiative minus 10. You can't use this feature when you are surprised.

subclasses.name: Assassin
subclasses.description: You focus your training on the grim art of death. Those who adhere to this archetype are diverse: hired killers, spies, bounty hunters, and even specially anointed priests trained to exterminate the enemies of their deity. Hallmark: surprise rounds make your day — automatic crit on a surprised target.

features.name: Bonus Proficiencies
features.body: When you choose this archetype at 3rd level, you gain proficiency with the disguise kit and the poisoner's kit.

features.name: Assassinate
features.body: Starting at 3rd level, you are at your deadliest when you get the drop on your enemies. You have advantage on attack rolls against any creature that hasn't taken a turn in the combat yet. In addition, any hit you score against a creature that is surprised is a critical hit.

features.name: Infiltration Expertise
features.body: Starting at 9th level, you can unfailingly create false identities for yourself. You must spend seven days and 25 gp to establish the history, profession, and affiliations for an identity. You can't establish an identity that belongs to someone else.

features.name: Impostor
features.body: At 13th level, you gain the ability to unerringly mimic another person's speech, writing, and behavior. You must spend at least three hours studying these three components of the person's behavior, listening to speech, examining handwriting, and observing mannerisms.

features.name: Death Strike
features.body: Starting at 17th level, you become a master of instant death. When you attack and hit a creature that is surprised, it must make a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 + your Dexterity modifier + your proficiency bonus). On a failed save, double the damage of your attack against the creature.

subclasses.name: Arcane Trickster
subclasses.description: A rogue who augments cunning with arcane illusion and enchantment magic. A third-caster: wizard cantrips and 1st-level spells from L3, with spell slots scaling on the third-caster table. Mage Hand Legerdemain turns the cantrip into a remote-controlled thief's hand. (INT-based casting + the wizard spell-list pool aren't yet surfaced in the creation wizard's Spells step — tracked under the third-caster follow-up.)

features.name: Spellcasting
features.body: When you reach 3rd level, you augment your rogue's cunning with magic from the wizard's spell list. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability. You learn three cantrips (one must be mage hand) and three 1st-level spells (two from enchantment or illusion, one from any school). Spell slots follow the third-caster table.

features.name: Mage Hand Legerdemain
features.body: Starting at 3rd level, when you cast mage hand, you can make the spectral hand invisible, and you can perform the following additional tasks with it: stow one object the hand is holding in a container worn or carried by another creature; retrieve an object in a container worn or carried by another creature; use thieves' tools to pick locks and disarm traps at range. You can perform one of these tasks without being noticed by a creature if you succeed on a Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check contested by the creature's Wisdom (Perception) check.

features.name: Magical Ambush
features.body: Starting at 9th level, if you are hidden from a creature when you cast a spell on it, the creature has disadvantage on any saving throw it makes against the spell this turn.

features.name: Versatile Trickster
features.body: At 13th level, you gain the ability to distract targets with your mage hand. As a bonus action on your turn, you can designate a creature within 5 feet of the spectral hand created by the spell. Doing so gives you advantage on attack rolls against that creature until the end of the turn.

features.name: Spell Thief
features.body: At 17th level, you gain the ability to magically steal the knowledge of how to cast a spell from another spellcaster. Immediately after a creature casts a spell that targets you or includes you in its area of effect, you can use your reaction to force the creature to make a saving throw with its spellcasting ability modifier (DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Intelligence modifier). On a failed save, you negate the spell's effect against you, and you steal the knowledge of the spell if it is at least 1st level and of a level you can cast. For the next 8 hours, you know the spell and can cast it using your spell slots. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

name: Barbarian
description: A fierce warrior of primitive background who can enter a battle rage.

features.name: Rage
features.body: On your turn, you can enter a rage as a bonus action. Your rage lasts for 1 minute and ends early if you fall unconscious, are knocked unconscious, or end your turn without attacking a hostile creature or taking damage since your last turn. While raging you gain advantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws, bonus damage on melee weapon attacks using Strength (+2 at 1st, +3 at 9th, +4 at 16th), and resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage. Uses per long rest: 2 (1st), 3 (3rd), 4 (6th), 5 (12th), 6 (17th), unlimited (20th).

features.name: Unarmored Defense
features.body: While you are not wearing any armor, your Armor Class equals 10 + your Dexterity modifier + your Constitution modifier. You can use a shield and still gain this benefit.

features.name: Reckless Attack
features.body: When you make your first attack on your turn, you can decide to attack recklessly. Doing so gives you advantage on melee weapon attack rolls using Strength during this turn, but attack rolls against you have advantage until your next turn.

features.name: Danger Sense
features.body: You have an uncanny sense of when things nearby aren't as they should be. You have advantage on Dexterity saving throws against effects that you can see, such as traps and spells. To gain this benefit, you can't be blinded, deafened, or incapacitated.

features.name: Primal Path
features.body: Choose a path that shapes the nature of your rage (Path of the Berserker or Path of the Totem Warrior). Your choice grants you features at 3rd level and again at 6th, 10th, and 14th level.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.body: You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase a score above 20 using this feature. You can instead take a feat.

features.name: Extra Attack
features.body: You can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

features.name: Fast Movement
features.body: Your speed increases by 10 feet while you aren't wearing heavy armor.

features.name: Feral Instinct
features.body: Your instincts are so honed that you have advantage on initiative rolls. Additionally, if you are surprised at the beginning of combat and aren't incapacitated, you can act normally on your first turn, but only if you enter your rage before doing anything else on that turn.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.body: You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase a score above 20 using this feature. You can instead take a feat.

features.name: Brutal Critical
features.body: You can roll one additional weapon damage die when determining the extra damage for a critical hit with a melee attack. This increases to two additional dice at 13th level and three additional dice at 17th level.

features.name: Relentless Rage
features.body: Your rage can keep you fighting despite grievous wounds. If you drop to 0 hit points while you're raging and don't die outright, you can make a DC 10 Constitution saving throw. If you succeed, you drop to 1 hit point instead. Each time you use this feature after the first, the DC increases by 5. The DC resets to 10 when you finish a short or long rest.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.body: You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase a score above 20 using this feature. You can instead take a feat.

features.name: Brutal Critical (2 dice)
features.body: You roll two additional weapon damage dice on a critical hit with a melee attack.

features.name: Persistent Rage
features.body: Your rage is so fierce that it ends early only if you fall unconscious or if you choose to end it.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.body: You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase a score above 20 using this feature. You can instead take a feat.

features.name: Brutal Critical (3 dice)
features.body: You roll three additional weapon damage dice on a critical hit with a melee attack.

features.name: Indomitable Might
features.body: If your total for a Strength check is less than your Strength score, you can use that score in place of the total.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.body: You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase a score above 20 using this feature. You can instead take a feat.

features.name: Primal Champion
features.body: You embody the power of the wilds. Your Strength and Constitution scores increase by 4. Your maximum for those scores is now 24.

features.name: Primal Knowledge
features.body: Tasha's optional feature: at 3rd level you gain proficiency in one skill of your choice from the list of skills available to barbarians at 1st level (Animal Handling, Athletics, Intimidation, Nature, Perception, Survival). You gain proficiency in one additional skill from that list at 10th level. Pick the skill manually on the Skills step for now — a Tasha's-knowledge skill picker is a follow-up.

subclasses.name: Path of the Berserker
subclasses.description: For some barbarians, rage is a means to an end — that end being violence. The Path of the Berserker is a path of untrammeled fury, slick with blood. Berserkers trade exhaustion for the heaviest single-target output the class can muster.

features.name: Frenzy
features.body: Starting when you choose this path at 3rd level, you can go into a frenzy when you rage. If you do so, for the duration of your rage you can make a single melee weapon attack as a bonus action on each of your turns after this one. When your rage ends, you suffer one level of exhaustion (as described in appendix A).

features.name: Mindless Rage
features.body: Beginning at 6th level, you can't be charmed or frightened while raging. If you are charmed or frightened when you enter your rage, the effect is suspended for the duration of the rage.

features.name: Intimidating Presence
features.body: Beginning at 10th level, you can use your action to frighten someone with your menacing presence. When you do so, choose one creature that you can see within 30 feet of you. If the creature can see or hear you, it must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw (DC equal to 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Charisma modifier) or be frightened of you until the end of your next turn. On subsequent turns, you can use your action to extend the duration of this effect on the frightened creature until the end of your next turn. This effect ends if the creature ends its turn out of line of sight or more than 60 feet away from you.

features.name: Retaliation
features.body: Starting at 14th level, when you take damage from a creature that is within 5 feet of you, you can use your reaction to make a melee weapon attack against that creature.

subclasses.name: Path of the Totem Warrior
subclasses.description: A barbarian who walks the spiritual path of the animal world, taking guardians and aspects from totem beasts. Hallmark: a CON-based defender — Bear totem resistance to nearly everything makes the totem warrior the table's incoming-damage sponge.

features.name: Spirit Seeker
features.body: Yours is a path that seeks attunement with the natural world, giving you a kinship with beasts. At 3rd level, you gain the ability to cast the beast sense and speak with animals spells, but only as rituals.

features.name: Totem Spirit
features.body: At 3rd level, when you adopt this path, you choose a totem spirit and gain its feature. Bear: while raging, you have resistance to all damage except psychic damage. Eagle: while raging, opportunity attacks against you have disadvantage, and you can use the Dash action as a bonus action. Wolf: while raging, your friends have advantage on melee attack rolls against any creature within 5 feet of you. Pick one — track which totem you chose manually for now.

features.name: Aspect of the Beast
features.body: At 6th level, you gain a magical benefit based on the totem animal of your choice (can differ from your 3rd-level pick). Bear: carrying capacity doubled + advantage on STR checks to push/pull/lift/break objects. Eagle: see clearly up to 1 mile; perceive in dim light as bright. Wolf: tracking expert + lead allies through difficult terrain at full speed if no larger than Medium. Pick one — narrative for now.

features.name: Spirit Walker
features.body: At 10th level, you can cast the commune with nature spell, but only as a ritual. When you do so, a spiritual version of one of the animals you chose for Totem Spirit or Aspect of the Beast appears to give you the information.

features.name: Totemic Attunement
features.body: At 14th level, you gain a magical benefit based on a totem animal of your choice. Bear: while raging, creatures within 5 feet that are hostile have disadvantage on attack rolls against creatures other than you. Eagle: while raging, you gain a flying speed equal to your walking speed. Wolf: while raging, when you knock a Large or smaller creature prone with a melee attack on your turn, you can use a bonus action to make a melee attack against that creature. Pick one — narrative.

name: Paladin
description: A holy warrior bound to a sacred oath.

features.name: Divine Sense
features.body: As an action, you can open your awareness to detect celestials, fiends, and undead within 60 feet. You can use this feature a number of times equal to 1 + your Charisma modifier per long rest.

features.name: Lay on Hands
features.body: You have a pool of healing power that replenishes each long rest. With that pool, you can restore a total number of hit points equal to your paladin level × 5. As an action, you can touch a creature and draw from the pool to restore hit points or to cure a disease or poison (5 points per disease/poison cured).

features.name: Fighting Style
features.body: You adopt a style of fighting as your specialty. Choose one: Defense (+1 AC while wearing armor), Dueling (+2 damage with one-handed melee weapons when no other weapon is held), Great Weapon Fighting (reroll 1s and 2s on damage dice for two-handed melee weapons), or Protection (impose disadvantage on an attack against a creature within 5 ft as a reaction).

features.name: Spellcasting
features.body: You have learnt to draw on divine magic through meditation and prayer to cast spells as a cleric does. Charisma is your spellcasting ability. You prepare a list of paladin spells available to cast equal to your Charisma modifier + half your paladin level (minimum one).

features.name: Divine Smite
features.body: When you hit a creature with a melee weapon attack, you can expend one paladin spell slot to deal radiant damage to the target, in addition to the weapon's damage. The extra damage is 2d8 for a 1st-level slot, plus 1d8 for each spell level higher than 1st, to a maximum of 5d8. The damage increases by 1d8 if the target is an undead or a fiend, to a maximum of 6d8.

features.name: Divine Health
features.body: By 3rd level, the divine magic flowing through you makes you immune to disease.

features.name: Sacred Oath
features.body: Choose your oath (Oath of Devotion, Oath of the Ancients, or Oath of Vengeance). Your choice grants you features at 3rd level and again at 7th, 15th, and 20th level. It also grants you Channel Divinity options and Oath Spells unique to your oath.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.body: You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase a score above 20 using this feature. You can instead take a feat.

features.name: Extra Attack
features.body: You can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

features.name: Aura of Protection
