features.body: Whenever you or a friendly creature within 10 feet of you must make a saving throw, the creature gains a bonus to the saving throw equal to your Charisma modifier (with a minimum bonus of +1). You must be conscious to grant this bonus. At 18th level, the range of this aura increases to 30 feet.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.body: You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase a score above 20 using this feature. You can instead take a feat.

features.name: Aura of Courage
features.body: You and friendly creatures within 10 feet of you can't be frightened while you are conscious. At 18th level, the range of this aura increases to 30 feet.

features.name: Improved Divine Smite
features.body: You are so suffused with righteous might that all your melee weapon strikes carry divine power with them. Whenever you hit a creature with a melee weapon, the creature takes an extra 1d8 radiant damage.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.body: You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase a score above 20 using this feature. You can instead take a feat.

features.name: Cleansing Touch
features.body: You can use your action to end one spell on yourself or on one willing creature that you touch. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (a minimum of once). You regain expended uses when you finish a long rest.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.body: You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase a score above 20 using this feature. You can instead take a feat.

features.name: Aura Improvements
features.body: The range of your Aura of Protection and Aura of Courage increases to 30 feet.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.body: You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase a score above 20 using this feature. You can instead take a feat.

features.name: Channel Divinity: Harness Divine Power
features.body: Tasha's optional Channel Divinity: as a bonus action, you draw on the divine to recover one spell slot of your choice from a level no higher than half your proficiency bonus (rounded up). Once you use this Channel Divinity, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest unless you expend a 1st-level spell slot to use it again.

subclasses.name: Oath of Devotion
subclasses.description: The classic knight in shining armor. The Oath of Devotion binds a paladin to the loftiest ideals of justice, virtue, and order. Hallmark: anti-undead/fiend tools and a charm-proof aura around the party.

features.name: Channel Divinity: Sacred Weapon
features.body: As an action, you can imbue one weapon that you are holding with positive energy, using your Channel Divinity. For 1 minute, you add your Charisma modifier to attack rolls made with that weapon (with a minimum bonus of +1). The weapon also emits bright light in a 20-foot radius and dim light 20 feet beyond that. If the weapon is not already magical, it becomes magical for the duration. You can end this effect on your turn as part of any other action.

features.name: Channel Divinity: Turn the Unholy
features.body: As an action, you present your holy symbol and speak a prayer censuring fiends and undead. Each fiend or undead that can see or hear you within 30 feet of you must make a Wisdom saving throw. If the creature fails, it is turned for 1 minute or until it takes damage.

features.name: Aura of Devotion
features.body: Starting at 7th level, you and friendly creatures within 10 feet of you can't be charmed while you are conscious. At 18th level, the range of this aura increases to 30 feet.

features.name: Purity of Spirit
features.body: Beginning at 15th level, you are always under the effects of a protection from evil and good spell.

features.name: Holy Nimbus
features.body: At 20th level, as an action, you can emanate an aura of sunlight. For 1 minute, bright light shines from you in a 30-foot radius, and dim light shines 30 feet beyond that. Whenever an enemy creature starts its turn in the bright light, the creature takes 10 radiant damage. In addition, for the duration, you have advantage on saving throws against spells cast by fiends or undead. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

subclasses.name: Oath of the Ancients
subclasses.description: The Oath of the Ancients is as old as the race of elves and the rituals of the druids. Sometimes called fey knights, green knights, or horned knights, paladins who swear this oath cast their lot with the side of the light in the cosmic struggle against darkness. Hallmark: spell-resistance aura makes the whole party a magic sponge.

features.name: Channel Divinity: Nature's Wrath
features.body: You can use your Channel Divinity to invoke primeval forces to ensnare a foe. As an action, you can cause spectral vines to spring up and reach for a creature within 10 feet of you that you can see. The creature must succeed on a Strength or Dexterity saving throw (its choice) or be restrained. While restrained by the vines, the creature repeats the saving throw at the end of each of its turns. On a success, it frees itself and the vines vanish.

features.name: Channel Divinity: Turn the Faithless
features.body: You can use your Channel Divinity to utter ancient words that are painful for fey and fiends to hear. As an action, you present your holy symbol, and each fey or fiend within 30 feet of you that can hear you must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the creature is turned for 1 minute or until it takes damage. A turned creature must spend its turns trying to move as far away from you as it can, and it can't willingly move to a space within 30 feet of you.

features.name: Aura of Warding
features.body: Starting at 7th level, ancient magic lies so heavily upon you that it forms an eldritch ward. You and friendly creatures within 10 feet of you have resistance to damage from spells. At 18th level, the range of this aura increases to 30 feet.

features.name: Undying Sentinel
features.body: Starting at 15th level, when you are reduced to 0 hit points and are not killed outright, you can choose to drop to 1 hit point instead. Once you use this ability, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest. Additionally, you suffer none of the drawbacks of old age and can't be aged magically.

features.name: Elder Champion
features.body: At 20th level, you can assume the form of an ancient force of nature, taking on an appearance you choose (e.g. green skin or bark-like skin). For 1 minute, you gain: regain 10 HP at the start of each of your turns; spells you cast with a casting time of 1 action take a bonus action instead; enemy creatures within 10 feet of you have disadvantage on saves against your paladin spells and Channel Divinity options. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

subclasses.name: Oath of Vengeance
subclasses.description: A grim oath that calls a paladin to punish those who have committed a grievous sin — sometimes called Avengers or Dark Knights. Hallmark: relentless single-target hunters with the Vow of Enmity Channel Divinity granting advantage on every attack against the marked foe.

features.name: Channel Divinity: Abjure Enemy
features.body: As an action, you present your holy symbol and speak a prayer of denunciation, using your Channel Divinity. Choose one creature within 60 feet of you that you can see. That creature must make a Wisdom saving throw, unless it is immune to being frightened. Fiends and undead have disadvantage on this saving throw. On a failed save, the creature is frightened for 1 minute or until it takes any damage. While frightened, the creature's speed is 0 and it can't benefit from any bonus to its speed. On a successful save, the creature's speed is halved for 1 minute or until the creature takes any damage.

features.name: Channel Divinity: Vow of Enmity
features.body: As a bonus action, you can utter a vow of enmity against a creature you can see within 10 feet of you, using your Channel Divinity. You gain advantage on attack rolls against the creature for 1 minute or until it drops to 0 hit points or falls unconscious.

features.name: Relentless Avenger
features.body: By 7th level, your supernatural focus helps you close off a foe's retreat. When you hit a creature with an opportunity attack, you can move up to half your speed immediately after the attack and as part of the same reaction. This movement doesn't provoke opportunity attacks.

features.name: Soul of Vengeance
features.body: Starting at 15th level, the authority with which you speak your Vow of Enmity gives you greater power over your foe. When a creature under the effect of your Vow of Enmity makes an attack, you can use your reaction to make a melee weapon attack against that creature if it is within range.

features.name: Avenging Angel
features.body: At 20th level, you can assume the form of an angelic avenger. Using your action, you undergo a transformation. For 1 hour, you gain the following benefits: wings sprout from your back and grant you a flying speed of 60 feet; you emanate an aura of menace in a 30-foot radius — the first time any enemy creature enters the aura or starts its turn there during a battle, the creature must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or be frightened for 1 minute or until it takes any damage. Attack rolls against the frightened creature have advantage. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

name: Bard
description: An inspiring magician whose power echoes the music of creation.
toolProficiencies: Three musical instruments of your choice

features.name: Spellcasting
features.body: You have learnt to untangle and reshape the fabric of reality in harmony with your wishes and music. Charisma is your spellcasting ability for your bard spells.

features.name: Bardic Inspiration
features.body: As a bonus action, you can choose one creature other than yourself within 60 feet who can hear you. That creature gains one Bardic Inspiration die. Within the next 10 minutes, the creature can roll the die and add the number to one ability check, attack roll, or saving throw it makes. The die is a d6 at 1st level, a d8 at 5th, a d10 at 10th, and a d12 at 15th. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (a minimum of once), and you regain expended uses on a long rest (a short rest from 5th level on).

features.name: Jack of All Trades
features.body: You can add half your proficiency bonus, rounded down, to any ability check you make that doesn't already include your proficiency bonus.

features.name: Song of Rest
features.body: You can use soothing music or oration during a short rest. If you or any friendly creatures who can hear your performance regain hit points at the end of the short rest by spending one or more Hit Dice, each of those creatures regains an extra 1d6 hit points. The extra hit points increase to 1d8 at 9th level, 1d10 at 13th, and 1d12 at 17th.

features.name: Bard College
features.body: Choose a bard college that grants you features at 3rd level and again at 6th and 14th level (College of Lore or College of Valor).

features.name: Expertise
features.body: Choose two of your skill proficiencies. Your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check you make that uses either of the chosen proficiencies. At 10th level, you can choose another two skill proficiencies to gain this benefit.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.body: You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase a score above 20 using this feature. You can instead take a feat.

features.name: Font of Inspiration
features.body: You regain all of your expended uses of Bardic Inspiration when you finish a short or long rest.

features.name: Countercharm
features.body: As an action, you can start a performance that lasts until the end of your next turn. During that time, you and any friendly creatures within 30 feet of you have advantage on saving throws against being frightened or charmed. A creature must be able to hear you to gain this benefit. The performance ends early if you are incapacitated or silenced or if you voluntarily end it.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.body: You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase a score above 20 using this feature. You can instead take a feat.

features.name: Magical Secrets
features.body: You have plundered magical knowledge from a wide spectrum of disciplines. Choose two spells from any class, including this one. A spell you choose must be of a level you can cast, or a cantrip. The chosen spells count as bard spells for you and are included in the number of spells you know. You learn two additional spells from any class at 14th level and again at 18th level.

features.name: Expertise (additional)
features.body: Choose another two of your skill proficiencies to gain expertise — your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check using those skills.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.body: You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase a score above 20 using this feature. You can instead take a feat.

features.name: Magical Secrets (additional)
features.body: You learn two additional spells from any class through Magical Secrets.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.body: You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase a score above 20 using this feature. You can instead take a feat.

features.name: Magical Secrets (additional)
features.body: You learn two additional spells from any class through Magical Secrets.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.body: You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase a score above 20 using this feature. You can instead take a feat.

features.name: Superior Inspiration
features.body: When you roll initiative and have no uses of Bardic Inspiration left, you regain one use.

features.name: Magical Inspiration
features.body: Tasha's optional feature: if a creature has a Bardic Inspiration die from you and casts a spell that restores hit points or deals damage, the creature can roll the die and choose a target — a creature damaged by the spell adds the result to a damage roll, or a creature healed by the spell adds the roll to one of its hit point totals. The Bardic Inspiration die is then lost.

subclasses.name: College of Lore
subclasses.description: Bards of the College of Lore know something about most things, collecting bits of knowledge wherever they wander. The college values the truth and seeks it out — useful skills, salient tales, and the precise word that unmakes another's confidence.

features.name: Bonus Proficiencies
features.body: When you join the College of Lore at 3rd level, you gain proficiency with three skills of your choice.

features.name: Cutting Words
features.body: Starting at 3rd level, you can use your wit to distract, confuse, and otherwise sap the confidence and competence of others. When a creature that you can see within 60 feet of you makes an attack roll, an ability check, or a damage roll, you can use your reaction to expend one of your uses of Bardic Inspiration, rolling a Bardic Inspiration die and subtracting the number rolled from the creature's roll. You can choose to use this feature after the creature makes its roll, but before the GM determines whether the attack roll or ability check succeeds or fails, or before the creature deals its damage. The creature is immune if it can't hear you or if it's immune to being charmed.

features.name: Additional Magical Secrets
features.body: At 6th level, you learn two spells of your choice from any class. A spell you choose must be of a level you can cast, as shown on the bard table, or a cantrip. The chosen spells count as bard spells for you but don't count against the number of bard spells you know.

features.name: Peerless Skill
features.body: Starting at 14th level, when you make an ability check, you can expend one use of Bardic Inspiration. Roll a Bardic Inspiration die and add the number rolled to your ability check. You can choose to do so after you roll the die for the ability check, but before the GM tells you whether you succeed or fail.

subclasses.name: College of Valor
subclasses.description: Bards of the College of Valor are daring skalds whose tales keep alive the memory of the great heroes of the past, and thereby inspire a new generation of heroes. These bards gather in mead halls or around great bonfires to sing of heroic deeds and stoke courage in the souls of warriors.

features.name: Bonus Proficiencies
features.body: When you join the College of Valor at 3rd level, you gain proficiency with medium armor, shields, and martial weapons.

features.name: Combat Inspiration
features.body: Also at 3rd level, you learn to inspire others in battle. A creature that has a Bardic Inspiration die from you can roll that die and add the number rolled to a weapon damage roll it just made. Alternatively, when an attack roll is made against the creature, it can use its reaction to roll the Bardic Inspiration die and add the number rolled to its AC against that attack, after seeing the roll but before knowing whether it hits or misses.

features.name: Extra Attack
features.body: Starting at 6th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

features.name: Battle Magic
features.body: At 14th level, you have mastered the art of weaving spellcasting and weapon use into a single harmonious act. When you use your action to cast a bard spell, you can make one weapon attack as a bonus action.

name: Druid
description: A priest of the Old Faith, wielding the powers of nature — moonlight and plant growth, fire and lightning — and adopting animal forms.

features.name: Druidic
features.body: You know Druidic, the secret language of druids. You can speak it and use it to leave hidden messages.

features.name: Spellcasting
features.body: Drawing on the divine essence of nature itself, you can cast spells to shape that essence to your will. Wisdom is your spellcasting ability. You prepare a list of druid spells equal to your Wisdom modifier + your druid level (minimum one).

features.name: Wild Shape
features.body: As an action, you can magically assume the shape of a beast that you have seen before. You can use this feature twice per short or long rest. You can stay in beast shape for hours equal to half your druid level. At 2nd level you can transform into a beast with a challenge rating of 1/4 or lower that has no flying or swimming speed. The CR limit increases as you level (see Wild Shape Improvement). You revert when the duration ends, when you fall unconscious, when you drop to 0 hit points, or when you use a bonus action to do so.

features.name: Druid Circle
features.body: Choose to identify with a circle of druids: the Circle of the Land or the Circle of the Moon. Your choice grants you features at 2nd level and again at 6th, 10th, and 14th level.

features.name: Wild Shape Improvement
features.body: You can now use your Wild Shape to transform into a beast with a challenge rating as high as 1/2 (no flying speed).

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.body: You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase a score above 20 using this feature. You can instead take a feat.

features.name: Wild Shape Improvement
features.body: You can now use your Wild Shape to transform into a beast with a challenge rating as high as 1, including beasts with a flying speed.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.body: You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase a score above 20 using this feature. You can instead take a feat.

features.body: You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase a score above 20 using this feature. You can instead take a feat.

features.body: You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase a score above 20 using this feature. You can instead take a feat.

features.name: Timeless Body
features.body: The primal magic that you wield causes you to age more slowly. For every 10 years that pass, your body ages only 1 year.

features.name: Beast Spells
features.body: You can cast many of your druid spells in any shape you assume using Wild Shape. You can perform the somatic and verbal components of a druid spell while in a beast shape, but not material components.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.body: You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase a score above 20 using this feature. You can instead take a feat.

features.name: Archdruid
features.body: You can use your Wild Shape an unlimited number of times. Additionally, you can ignore the verbal and somatic components of your druid spells, as well as any material components that lack a cost and aren't consumed by a spell.

features.name: Cantrip Versatility
features.body: Tasha's optional feature: whenever you finish a long rest, you can replace one druid cantrip you know with another cantrip from the druid spell list.

subclasses.name: Circle of the Land
subclasses.description: The Circle of the Land is made up of mystics and sages who safeguard ancient knowledge and rites through a vast oral tradition. These druids meet within sacred circles of trees or standing stones to whisper primal secrets in Druidic.

features.name: Bonus Cantrip
features.body: When you choose this circle at 2nd level, you learn one additional druid cantrip of your choice.

features.name: Natural Recovery
features.body: Starting at 2nd level, you can regain some of your magical energy by sitting in meditation and communing with nature. During a short rest, you choose expended spell slots to recover. The slots can have a combined level that is equal to or less than half your druid level (rounded up), and none of the slots can be 6th level or higher.

features.name: Circle Spells
features.body: Your mystical connection to the land infuses you with the ability to cast certain spells. At 3rd, 5th, 7th, and 9th level you gain access to circle spells connected to the land where you became a druid (arctic, coast, desert, forest, grassland, mountain, swamp, Underdark, or Underwater). Once you choose the associated land you can't change it. The circle spell list is added to your prepared spells and doesn't count against the number you can prepare. (Pick your land manually for now — the land-specific spell granter is a follow-up.)

features.name: Land's Stride
features.body: Starting at 6th level, moving through nonmagical difficult terrain costs you no extra movement. You can also pass through nonmagical plants without being slowed by them and without taking damage from them if they have thorns, spines, or a similar hazard. In addition, you have advantage on saving throws against plants that are magically created or manipulated to impede movement.

features.name: Nature's Ward
features.body: When you reach 10th level, you can't be charmed or frightened by elementals or fey, and you are immune to poison and disease.

features.name: Nature's Sanctuary
features.body: When you reach 14th level, creatures of the natural world sense your connection to nature and become hesitant to attack you. When a beast or plant creature attacks you, that creature must make a Wisdom saving throw against your druid spell save DC. On a failed save, the creature must choose a different target, or the attack automatically misses. On a successful save, the creature is immune to this effect for 24 hours.

subclasses.name: Circle of the Moon
subclasses.description: Druids of the Moon are fierce guardians of the wild. They walk paths of moonlight and wear forms of swift and savage beasts. Hallmark: turn into beasts much earlier and much bigger than other druids, and use Wild Shape as a combat resource.

features.name: Combat Wild Shape
features.body: When you choose this circle at 2nd level, you gain the ability to use Wild Shape on your turn as a bonus action, rather than as an action. Additionally, while you are transformed by Wild Shape, you can use a bonus action to expend one spell slot to regain 1d8 hit points per level of the spell slot expended.

features.name: Circle Forms
features.body: The rites of your circle grant you the ability to transform into more dangerous animal forms. Starting at 2nd level, you can use your Wild Shape to transform into a beast with a challenge rating as high as 1. You ignore the Max. CR column of the Beast Shapes table, but must abide by the other limitations there. Starting at 6th level, you can transform into a beast with a challenge rating as high as your druid level divided by 3, rounded down.

features.name: Primal Strike
features.body: Starting at 6th level, your attacks in beast form count as magical for the purpose of overcoming resistance and immunity to nonmagical attacks and damage.

features.name: Elemental Wild Shape
features.body: At 10th level, you can expend two uses of Wild Shape at the same time to transform into an air elemental, an earth elemental, a fire elemental, or a water elemental.

features.name: Thousand Forms
features.body: By 14th level, you have learned to use magic to alter your physical form in more subtle ways. You can cast the alter self spell at will.

name: Monk
description: A master of martial arts, harnessing the power of the body in pursuit of physical and spiritual perfection.
toolProficiencies: One type of artisan's tools or one musical instrument

features.name: Unarmored Defense
features.body: While you are wearing no armor and not wielding a shield, your AC equals 10 + your Dexterity modifier + your Wisdom modifier.

features.name: Martial Arts
features.body: Your practice of martial arts gives you mastery of combat styles that use unarmed strikes and monk weapons. You can use Dexterity instead of Strength for the attack and damage rolls of your unarmed strikes and monk weapons. You can roll a martial-arts die in place of the normal damage (d4 at 1st, d6 at 5th, d8 at 11th, d10 at 17th). When you take the Attack action with an unarmed strike or a monk weapon, you can make one unarmed strike as a bonus action.

features.name: Ki
features.body: Your training allows you to harness the mystic energy of ki. Your access to this energy is represented by a number of ki points (equal to your monk level). You can spend these points to fuel various ki features (Flurry of Blows, Patient Defense, Step of the Wind), regaining all expended ki on a short or long rest. Save DC for ki features = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Wisdom modifier.

features.name: Unarmored Movement
features.body: Your speed increases by 10 feet while you are not wearing armor or wielding a shield. The bonus increases when you reach certain monk levels: +15 ft at 6th, +20 ft at 10th, +25 ft at 14th, +30 ft at 18th.

features.name: Monastic Tradition
features.body: Choose a monastic tradition (Way of the Open Hand, Way of Shadow, or Way of the Four Elements). Your choice grants you features at 3rd level and again at 6th, 11th, and 17th level.

features.name: Deflect Missiles
features.body: You can use your reaction to deflect or catch a missile when you are hit by a ranged weapon attack. The damage you take is reduced by 1d10 + your Dexterity modifier + your monk level. If you reduce the damage to 0 and the missile is small enough, you can catch it and spend 1 ki point to throw it back as a ranged attack.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.body: You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase a score above 20 using this feature. You can instead take a feat.

features.name: Slow Fall
features.body: You can use your reaction when you fall to reduce any falling damage you take by an amount equal to five times your monk level.

features.name: Extra Attack
features.body: You can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

features.name: Stunning Strike
features.body: You can interfere with the flow of ki in an opponent's body. When you hit another creature with a melee weapon attack, you can spend 1 ki point to attempt a stunning strike. The target must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or be stunned until the end of your next turn.

features.name: Ki-Empowered Strikes
features.body: Your unarmed strikes count as magical for the purpose of overcoming resistance and immunity to nonmagical attacks and damage.

features.name: Evasion
features.body: Your instinctive agility lets you dodge out of the way of certain area effects, such as a blue dragon's breath or a fireball spell. When subjected to an effect that allows a Dex save for half damage, you take no damage on a success and only half on a failure.

features.name: Stillness of Mind
features.body: You can use your action to end one effect on yourself that is causing you to be charmed or frightened.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.body: You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase a score above 20 using this feature. You can instead take a feat.

features.name: Unarmored Movement Improvement
features.body: You gain the ability to move along vertical surfaces and across liquids on your turn without falling during the move.

features.name: Purity of Body
features.body: Your mastery of ki suffuses your body with vigor: you are immune to disease and poison.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.body: You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase a score above 20 using this feature. You can instead take a feat.

features.name: Tongue of the Sun and Moon
features.body: You learn to touch the ki of other minds so that you understand all spoken languages. Moreover, any creature that can understand a language can understand what you say.

features.name: Diamond Soul
features.body: Your mastery of ki grants you proficiency in all saving throws. Additionally, whenever you make a saving throw and fail, you can spend 1 ki point to reroll it and take the second result.

features.name: Timeless Body
features.body: Your ki sustains you so that you suffer none of the frailty of old age, and you can't be aged magically. You no longer need food or water.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.body: You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase a score above 20 using this feature. You can instead take a feat.

features.name: Empty Body
features.body: You can use your action to spend 4 ki points to become invisible for 1 minute. During that time, you also have resistance to all damage but force damage. Additionally, you can spend 8 ki points to cast astral projection without needing material components. When you do so, you can't take any other creatures with you.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.body: You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase a score above 20 using this feature. You can instead take a feat.

features.name: Perfect Self
features.body: When you roll initiative and have no ki points remaining, you regain 4 ki points.

features.name: Dedicated Weapon
features.body: Tasha's optional feature: whenever you finish a short or long rest, you can touch one weapon, provided it is not a heavy weapon, and that you are proficient with it. When you attack with that weapon, you can use your Dexterity instead of Strength for the attack and damage rolls, and the weapon's damage die counts as your Martial Arts die. The effect ends if you later use this feature on a different weapon, or if you don any armor or wield a shield.

features.name: Ki-Fueled Attack
features.body: Tasha's optional feature: if you spend 1 ki point or more as part of your action on your turn, you can make one attack with an unarmed strike or monk weapon as a bonus action before the end of your turn.

features.name: Quickened Healing
features.body: Tasha's optional feature: as a bonus action, you can spend 2 ki points and roll your martial arts die. You regain a number of hit points equal to the number rolled + your proficiency bonus.

subclasses.name: Way of the Open Hand
subclasses.description: The classic martial-arts master. Specialise in striking down foes, both with mystic chi and a flurry of well-aimed blows. Manipulate the energies in your body to heal and survive what others can't.

features.name: Open Hand Technique
features.body: Starting when you choose this tradition at 3rd level, you can manipulate your enemy's ki when you harness your own. Whenever you hit a creature with one of the attacks granted by your Flurry of Blows, you can impose one of the following effects on that target: it must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or be knocked prone; it must make a Strength saving throw — fail, and you push it up to 15 feet away from you; it can't take reactions until the end of your next turn.

features.name: Wholeness of Body
features.body: At 6th level, you gain the ability to heal yourself. As an action, you can regain hit points equal to three times your monk level. You must finish a long rest before you can use this feature again.

features.name: Tranquility
features.body: At 11th level, you can enter a special meditation that surrounds you with an aura of peace. At the end of a long rest, you gain the effect of a sanctuary spell that lasts until the start of your next long rest (the spell can end early as normal). The saving throw DC for the spell equals 8 + your Wisdom modifier + your proficiency bonus.

features.name: Quivering Palm
features.body: At 17th level, you gain the ability to set up lethal vibrations in someone's body. When you hit a creature with an unarmed strike, you can spend 3 ki points to start these imperceptible vibrations, which last for a number of days equal to your monk level. The vibrations are harmless unless you use your action to end them. To do so, you and the target must be on the same plane of existence. When you use this action, the creature must make a Constitution saving throw. If it fails, it is reduced to 0 hit points. If it succeeds, it takes 10d10 necrotic damage. You can have only one creature under the effect of this feature at a time. You can choose to end the vibrations harmlessly without using an action.

subclasses.name: Way of Shadow
subclasses.description: Monks of the Way of Shadow follow a tradition that values stealth and subterfuge. These monks might be called ninjas or shadowdancers, and they serve as spies and assassins. Hallmark: ki-fuelled stealth spells, teleport-between-shadows, and ambushes from impossible angles.

features.name: Shadow Arts
features.body: Starting when you choose this tradition at 3rd level, you can use your ki to duplicate the effects of certain spells. As an action, you can spend 2 ki points to cast darkness, darkvision, pass without trace, or silence, without providing material components. Additionally, you gain the minor illusion cantrip if you don't already know it.

features.name: Shadow Step
features.body: At 6th level, you gain the ability to step from one shadow into another. When you are in dim light or darkness, as a bonus action you can teleport up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space you can see that is also in dim light or darkness. You then have advantage on the first melee attack you make before the end of the turn.

features.name: Cloak of Shadows
features.body: By 11th level, you have learned to become one with the shadows. When you are in an area of dim light or darkness, you can use your action to become invisible. You remain invisible until you make an attack, cast a spell, or are in an area of bright light.

features.name: Opportunist
features.body: At 17th level, you can exploit a creature's momentary distraction when it is hit by an attack. Whenever a creature within 5 feet of you is hit by an attack made by a creature other than you, you can use your reaction to make a melee attack against that creature.

subclasses.name: Way of the Four Elements
subclasses.description: Monks who follow the Way of the Four Elements channel elemental forces through their ki — elemental disciplines that spend ki points to unleash short bursts of fire, water, air, or earth magic. The signature monk gish. (Discipline picks are narrative for now — they spend the existing ki pool but aren't itemised as separate counters.)

features.name: Disciple of the Elements
features.body: When you choose this tradition at 3rd level, you learn magical disciplines that harness the power of the four elements. A discipline requires you to spend ki points each time you use it. You know the Elemental Attunement discipline plus one other discipline of your choice. You learn one additional elemental discipline of your choice at 6th, 11th, and 17th level. Whenever you learn a new elemental discipline, you can also replace one elemental discipline that you already know with a different discipline. The DC for any saving throws caused by an elemental discipline = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Wisdom modifier.

features.name: Casting Elemental Spells
features.body: Some elemental disciplines allow you to cast spells. The maximum number of ki points you can spend to cast a spell scales with monk level: 5 ki by L5 (spell L1–2), 6 ki by L9 (up to spell L3), 7 ki by L13 (up to spell L4), 9 ki by L17 (up to spell L5). You must spend an additional ki point for each level of the spell beyond its base — for example, casting Fireball at 4th level costs 7 ki points. The maximum ki points you can spend on a single spell is limited by the table above.

features.name: Elemental Adept
features.body: By 17th level, your elemental disciplines are at their full power: you have access to disciplines requiring up to 9 ki points to use, you can cast monk-list elemental spells up to 5th level, and you've added Breath of Winter / Eternal Mountain Defense / River of Hungry Flame / Wave of Rolling Earth to the disciplines you can learn.

name: Ranger
description: A warrior who uses martial prowess and nature magic to combat threats on the edges of civilisation.

features.name: Favored Enemy
features.body: Choose a type of favored enemy (aberrations, beasts, celestials, constructs, dragons, elementals, fey, fiends, giants, monstrosities, oozes, plants, or undead; or two races of humanoid). You have advantage on Wisdom (Survival) checks to track your favored enemies and on Intelligence checks to recall information about them. You also learn one language of your choice spoken by your favored enemies.

features.name: Natural Explorer
features.body: Choose one type of favored terrain (arctic, coast, desert, forest, grassland, mountain, swamp, or the Underdark). While travelling for an hour or more in your favored terrain you gain many benefits: difficult terrain doesn't slow your group, your group can't become lost except by magical means, you remain alert to danger while doing another activity, you can move stealthily at a normal pace while alone, you find twice as much food while foraging, and you learn the exact number, sizes, and how long ago creatures passed while tracking them.

features.name: Fighting Style
features.body: You adopt a fighting style as your specialty. Choose one: Archery (+2 to attack rolls with ranged weapons), Defense (+1 AC while wearing armor), Dueling (+2 damage with one-handed melee weapons when no other weapon is held), or Two-Weapon Fighting (add ability modifier to off-hand damage).

features.name: Spellcasting
features.body: By the time you reach 2nd level, you have learnt to use the magical essence of nature to cast spells. Wisdom is your spellcasting ability. You prepare a list of ranger spells equal to your Wisdom modifier + half your ranger level (minimum one).

features.name: Ranger Archetype
features.body: Choose an archetype that you strive to emulate (Hunter or Beast Master). Your choice grants you features at 3rd level and again at 7th, 11th, and 15th level.

features.name: Primeval Awareness
features.body: You can use your action and expend one ranger spell slot to focus your awareness on the region around you. For 1 minute per level of the spell slot expended, you can sense whether the following types of creatures are present within 1 mile of you (or 6 miles in your favored terrain): aberrations, celestials, dragons, elementals, fey, fiends, and undead.

features.body: You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase a score above 20 using this feature. You can instead take a feat.

features.name: Extra Attack
features.body: You can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

features.name: Favored Enemy (additional)
features.body: Choose one additional favored enemy and one additional language spoken by your favored enemies.

features.name: Natural Explorer (additional)
features.body: Choose one additional favored terrain to apply Natural Explorer to.

You can also pass through nonmagical plants without being slowed by them and without taking damage from them if they have thorns, spines, or a similar hazard. In addition, you have advantage on saving throws against plants that are magically created or manipulated to impede movement, such as those created by entangle.

features.name: Hide in Plain Sight
features.body: You can spend 1 minute creating camouflage for yourself. You must have access to fresh mud, dirt, plants, soot, and other naturally occurring materials. Once camouflaged, you gain a +10 bonus to Dexterity (Stealth) checks as long as you remain there without moving or taking actions.

features.name: Natural Explorer (third)
features.body: Choose one additional favored terrain to apply Natural Explorer to.

features.body: You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase a score above 20 using this feature. You can instead take a feat.

features.name: Favored Enemy (third)
features.body: Choose one additional favored enemy and one additional language spoken by your favored enemies.

features.name: Vanish
features.body: You can use the Hide action as a bonus action on your turn. Also, you can't be tracked by nonmagical means, unless you choose to leave a trail.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.body: You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase a score above 20 using this feature. You can instead take a feat.

features.name: Feral Senses
features.body: When you attack a creature you can't see, your inability to see it doesn't impose disadvantage on your attack rolls against it. You are also aware of the location of any invisible creature within 30 feet of you, provided that the creature isn't hidden from you and you aren't blinded or deafened.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.body: You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase a score above 20 using this feature. You can instead take a feat.

features.name: Foe Slayer
features.body: You become an unparalleled hunter of your enemies. Once on each of your turns, you can add your Wisdom modifier to the attack roll or the damage roll of an attack you make against one of your favored enemies. You can choose to use this feature before or after the roll, but before any effects of the roll are applied.

features.name: Deft Explorer
features.body: Tasha's alternative to Natural Explorer. You gain proficiency in one skill of your choice from the ranger's class skill list, plus one additional language. Additionally, you can move with little effort through difficult terrain — your speed isn't reduced by it. As you reach higher levels in this class, you gain extra Deft Explorer benefits (Roving at 6th, Tireless at 10th).

features.name: Favored Foe
features.body: Tasha's alternative to Favored Enemy. You can call on your bond with nature to mark a creature as your favored enemy for a time. As a bonus action, you can hunter's-mark a creature you can see within 30 feet (concentration up to 1 minute). The first time on each of your turns that you hit it with an attack, the target takes extra damage equal to one Favored Foe die (1d4 at L1, 1d6 at L6, 1d8 at L14). You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus per long rest.

subclasses.name: Hunter
subclasses.description: Emulating the Hunter archetype means accepting your place as a bulwark between civilization and the terrors of the wilderness. Pick-your-own kit of damage / defense / multi-attack options that adapts to whatever the table is fighting.

features.name: Hunter's Prey
features.body: At 3rd level, you gain one of the following features of your choice. Colossus Slayer: once per turn deal +1d8 to a creature below max HP. Giant Killer: when a Large+ creature within 5 ft hits or misses you, reaction to attack it. Horde Breaker: once per turn, when you make a weapon attack, make another attack against a different creature within 5 ft of the first using the same weapon. Pick one — track which one your character chose manually for now.

features.name: Defensive Tactics
features.body: At 7th level, you gain one of the following features of your choice. Escape the Horde: disadvantage on opportunity attacks against you. Multiattack Defense: when a creature hits you, +4 AC against further attacks from that creature this turn. Steel Will: advantage on saves vs being frightened. Pick one — track which one your character chose manually for now.

features.name: Multiattack
features.body: At 11th level, you gain one of the following features of your choice. Volley: ranged attack action targets all creatures in 10-ft radius. Whirlwind Attack: melee attack action targets all creatures in 5 ft. Pick one — track which one your character chose manually for now.

features.name: Superior Hunter's Defense
features.body: At 15th level, you gain one of the following features of your choice. Evasion: half damage on DEX saves that allow it; none on success. Stand Against the Tide: when a creature misses you with melee, reaction to redirect attack to another creature. Uncanny Dodge: reaction to halve damage from an attack you can see. Pick one — track manually.

subclasses.name: Beast Master
subclasses.description: Emulating the Beast Master archetype means committing yourself to a partnership with a wild creature. The two of you fight as a pair, your bond strengthening as you adventure together.

features.name: Ranger's Companion
features.body: At 3rd level, you bond with a beast of CR 1/4 or lower of Medium size or smaller. The companion gains your proficiency bonus added to its AC, attack rolls, damage rolls, and saving throws / skills it's proficient in. Its hit point maximum equals 4 × your ranger level (or its statblock total, whichever is higher). Use the Resources → Bind companion action to pick its species; the picker applies the HP boost automatically.

features.name: Exceptional Training
features.body: At 7th level, on any of your turns when your beast companion doesn't attack, you can use a bonus action to command it to take the Dash, Disengage, or Help action. Its attacks count as magical for the purpose of overcoming resistance and immunity to nonmagical attacks.

features.name: Bestial Fury
features.body: At 11th level, your beast companion can make two attacks when you command it to attack.

features.name: Share Spells
features.body: At 15th level, when you cast a spell targeting yourself, you can also have the spell affect your beast companion if it is within 30 feet of you.

name: Sorcerer
description: A spellcaster who draws on inherent magic from a gift or bloodline.

features.name: Spellcasting
features.body: An event in your past, or in the life of a parent or ancestor, left an indelible mark on you, infusing you with arcane magic. Charisma is your spellcasting ability.

features.name: Sorcerous Origin
features.body: Choose a sorcerous origin, which describes the source of your innate magical power (Draconic Bloodline or Wild Magic). Your choice grants you features at 1st level and again at 6th, 14th, and 18th level.

features.name: Font of Magic
features.body: You tap into a deep wellspring of magic within yourself, represented by sorcery points. Your sorcery point maximum equals your sorcerer level. You regain all expended sorcery points on a long rest. You can convert sorcery points into spell slots as a bonus action (or convert unused slots back into sorcery points).

features.name: Metamagic
features.body: You gain the ability to twist your spells to suit your needs. Choose two of the following Metamagic options: Careful Spell, Distant Spell, Empowered Spell, Extended Spell, Heightened Spell, Quickened Spell, Subtle Spell, or Twinned Spell. You gain another Metamagic option of your choice at 10th level and again at 17th level.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.body: You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase a score above 20 using this feature. You can instead take a feat.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.body: You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase a score above 20 using this feature. You can instead take a feat.

features.name: Metamagic (additional)
features.body: Choose one additional Metamagic option.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.body: You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase a score above 20 using this feature. You can instead take a feat.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.body: You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase a score above 20 using this feature. You can instead take a feat.

features.name: Metamagic (additional)
features.body: Choose one additional Metamagic option.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.body: You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase a score above 20 using this feature. You can instead take a feat.

features.name: Sorcerous Restoration
features.body: You regain 4 expended sorcery points whenever you finish a short rest.

features.name: Sorcerous Versatility
features.body: Tasha's optional feature: whenever you reach a level in this class that grants the Ability Score Improvement feature, you can replace one of the following options you have with another option of the same type: a cantrip you learned from this class's Spellcasting feature; one Metamagic option you know. Re-running the relevant Class step picker manually is the v1 workflow until the swap UI lands.

subclasses.name: Draconic Bloodline
subclasses.description: Your innate magic comes from draconic blood, latent in your veins. Most have a single ancestral dragon — chromatic or metallic — that gifts them an affinity for one damage type. Hallmark: tankier than a sorcerer should be, with bonus damage on every spell of your ancestral element.

features.name: Dragon Ancestor
features.body: At 1st level, you choose one type of dragon as your ancestor. The damage type associated with each dragon is used by features you gain later. (Black/Copper: acid, Blue/Bronze: lightning, Brass/Gold/Red: fire, Green: poison, Silver/White: cold.) You can speak, read, and write Draconic. Additionally, whenever you make a Charisma check when interacting with dragons, your proficiency bonus is doubled if it applies to the check.

features.name: Draconic Resilience
features.body: Your hit point maximum increases by 1 and increases by 1 again whenever you gain a level in this class. Additionally, parts of your skin are covered by a thin sheen of dragon-like scales. When you aren't wearing armor, your AC equals 13 + your Dexterity modifier.

features.name: Elemental Affinity
features.body: Starting at 6th level, when you cast a spell that deals damage of the type associated with your draconic ancestry, you can add your Charisma modifier to one damage roll of that spell. At the same time, you can spend 1 sorcery point to gain resistance to that damage type for 1 hour.

features.name: Dragon Wings
features.body: At 14th level, you gain the ability to sprout a pair of dragon wings from your back, gaining a flying speed equal to your current speed. You can create these wings as a bonus action on your turn. They last until you dismiss them as a bonus action on your turn. You can't manifest your wings while wearing armor unless the armor is made to accommodate them, and clothing not made to accommodate your wings might be destroyed when you manifest them.

features.name: Draconic Presence
features.body: Beginning at 18th level, you can channel the dread presence of your dragon ancestor, causing those around you to become awestruck or frightened. As an action, you can spend 5 sorcery points to draw on this power and exude an aura of awe or fear (your choice) to a distance of 60 feet. For 1 minute or until you lose your concentration (as if you were casting a concentration spell), each hostile creature that starts its turn in this aura must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or be charmed (if you chose awe) or frightened (if you chose fear) until the aura ends. A creature that succeeds on this saving throw is immune to your aura for 24 hours.

subclasses.name: Wild Magic
subclasses.description: Your innate magic comes from the wild forces of chaos that underlie the order of creation. Your spells let you nudge fate, the world's energy flowing through you in unpredictable ways. Hallmark: the wild magic surge table — every spell cast is a roll of the dice for a chaotic side effect.

features.name: Wild Magic Surge
features.body: Starting when you choose this origin at 1st level, your spellcasting can unleash surges of untamed magic. Immediately after you cast a sorcerer spell of 1st level or higher, the DM can have you roll a d20. If you roll a 1, roll on the Wild Magic Surge table to create a random magical effect. A Wild Magic Surge effect, if it's a spell, is too wild to be affected by your Metamagic. (Surge table is a DM-side reference for now; pick the result by hand.)

features.name: Tides of Chaos
features.body: Starting at 1st level, you can manipulate the forces of chance and chaos to gain advantage on one attack roll, ability check, or saving throw. Once you do so, you must finish a long rest before you can use this feature again. Any time before you regain the use of this feature, the DM can have you roll on the Wild Magic Surge table immediately after you cast a sorcerer spell of 1st level or higher. You then regain the use of this feature.

features.name: Bend Luck
features.body: Starting at 6th level, you have the ability to twist fate using your wild magic. When another creature you can see makes an attack roll, an ability check, or a saving throw, you can use your reaction and spend 2 sorcery points to roll 1d4 and apply the number rolled as a bonus or penalty (your choice) to the creature's roll. You can do so after the creature rolls but before any effects of the roll occur.

features.name: Controlled Chaos
features.body: At 14th level, you gain a modicum of control over the surges of your wild magic. Whenever you roll on the Wild Magic Surge table, you can roll twice and use either number.

features.name: Spell Bombardment
features.body: Beginning at 18th level, the harmful energy of your spells intensifies. When you roll damage for a spell and roll the highest number possible on any of the dice, choose one of those dice, roll it again, and add that roll to the damage. You can use the feature only once per turn.

name: Warlock
description: A wielder of magic that is derived from a bargain with an extraplanar entity.

features.name: Otherworldly Patron
features.body: You have struck a bargain with an otherworldly being of your choice — a Fiend, an Archfey, or a Great Old One. The choice grants you features at 1st level and again at 6th, 10th, and 14th level. It also grants you an Expanded Spell List.

features.name: Pact Magic
features.body: Your arcane research and the magic bestowed on you by your patron have given you facility with spells. Charisma is your spellcasting ability. Your pact slots recover on a short or long rest. Slot count and slot level both scale with warlock level (see the Warlock table).

features.name: Eldritch Invocations
features.body: In your study of occult lore, you have unearthed fragments of forbidden knowledge that imbue you with an abiding magical ability. At 2nd level, you gain two eldritch invocations of your choice. You gain additional invocations of your choice at higher levels (3 at 5th, 4 at 7th, 5 at 9th, 6 at 12th, 7 at 15th, and 8 at 18th). Additionally, when you gain a warlock level, you can choose one of the invocations you know and replace it with another invocation that you could learn.

features.name: Pact Boon
features.body: Your otherworldly patron bestows a gift upon you for your loyal service. You gain one of the following features of your choice: Pact of the Blade (summon a pact weapon), Pact of the Chain (gain the Find Familiar spell with extra forms), or Pact of the Tome (a Book of Shadows holding three extra cantrips).

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.body: You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase a score above 20 using this feature. You can instead take a feat.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.body: You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase a score above 20 using this feature. You can instead take a feat.

features.name: Mystic Arcanum (6th)
features.body: Your patron bestows upon you a magical secret called an arcanum. Choose one 6th-level warlock spell as this arcanum. You can cast it once without expending a spell slot. You must finish a long rest before you can do so again.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.body: You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase a score above 20 using this feature. You can instead take a feat.

features.name: Mystic Arcanum (7th)
features.body: Choose one 7th-level warlock spell as an arcanum. You can cast it once without expending a spell slot. You regain the ability to do so when you finish a long rest.

features.name: Mystic Arcanum (8th)
features.body: Choose one 8th-level warlock spell as an arcanum. You can cast it once without expending a spell slot. You regain the ability to do so when you finish a long rest.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.body: You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase a score above 20 using this feature. You can instead take a feat.

features.name: Mystic Arcanum (9th)
features.body: Choose one 9th-level warlock spell as an arcanum. You can cast it once without expending a spell slot. You regain the ability to do so when you finish a long rest.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.body: You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase a score above 20 using this feature. You can instead take a feat.

features.name: Eldritch Master
features.body: You can draw on your inner reserve of mystical power while entreating your patron to regain expended spell slots. You can spend 1 minute entreating your patron for aid to regain all your expended pact magic spell slots. Once you regain spell slots with this feature, you must finish a long rest before you can do so again.

features.name: Eldritch Versatility
features.body: Tasha's optional feature: whenever you reach a level in this class that grants the Ability Score Improvement feature, you can replace a cantrip you learned from this class's Pact Magic feature with another cantrip from the warlock spell list, OR replace one option you chose for the Pact Boon feature with another option, OR replace one Eldritch Invocation you know with another invocation you could learn at your current level. If this change makes a character option on your sheet invalid, that option must also be changed accordingly.

subclasses.name: The Archfey
subclasses.description: Your patron is a lord or lady of the fey — a creature of legend who holds secrets that were forgotten before the mortal races were born. Hallmark: charm tools that mid-fight bounce enemies away, and at higher tiers, fey-step out of trouble.

features.name: Expanded Spell List
features.body: The Archfey lets you choose from an expanded list of spells when you learn a warlock spell. The following spells are added to the warlock spell list for you: 1st — Faerie Fire, Sleep. 2nd — Calm Emotions, Phantasmal Force. 3rd — Blink, Plant Growth. 4th — Dominate Beast, Greater Invisibility. 5th — Dominate Person, Seeming.

features.name: Fey Presence
features.body: Starting at 1st level, your patron bestows upon you the ability to project the beguiling and fearsome presence of the fey. As an action, you can cause each creature in a 10-foot cube originating from you to make a Wisdom saving throw against your warlock spell save DC. The creatures that fail their saving throws are all charmed or frightened by you (your choice) until the end of your next turn. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

features.name: Misty Escape
features.body: Starting at 6th level, you can vanish in a puff of mist in response to harm. When you take damage, you can use your reaction to turn invisible and teleport up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space you can see. You remain invisible until the start of your next turn or until you attack or cast a spell. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

features.name: Beguiling Defenses
features.body: Beginning at 10th level, your patron teaches you how to turn the mind-affecting magic of your enemies against them. You are immune to being charmed, and when another creature attempts to charm you, you can use your reaction to attempt to turn the charm back on that creature. The creature must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your warlock spell save DC or be charmed by you for 1 minute or until the creature takes any damage.

features.name: Dark Delirium
features.body: Starting at 14th level, you can plunge a creature into an illusory realm. As an action, choose a creature that you can see within 60 feet of you. It must make a Wisdom saving throw against your warlock spell save DC. On a failed save, it is charmed or frightened by you (your choice) for 1 minute or until your concentration is broken (as if you are concentrating on a spell). This effect ends early if the creature takes any damage. While charmed or frightened, the creature thinks it is lost in a misty realm, the appearance of which you choose. The creature can see and hear only itself, you, and the illusion. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

subclasses.name: The Fiend
subclasses.description: You have made a pact with a fiend from the lower planes — a being whose aims are evil, even if you strive against those aims. The classic warlock patron: blasty, durable, and rewarded for blowing things up.

features.name: Dark One's Blessing
features.body: Starting at 1st level, when you reduce a hostile creature to 0 hit points, you gain temporary hit points equal to your Charisma modifier + your warlock level (minimum of 1).

features.name: Expanded Spell List
features.body: The Fiend lets you choose from an expanded list of spells when you learn a warlock spell. The following spells are added to the warlock spell list for you: 1st — Burning Hands, Command. 2nd — Blindness/Deafness, Scorching Ray. 3rd — Fireball, Stinking Cloud. 4th — Fire Shield, Wall of Fire. 5th — Flame Strike, Hallow.

features.name: Dark One's Own Luck
features.body: Starting at 6th level, you can call on your patron to alter fate in your favor. When you make an ability check or a saving throw, you can use this feature to add a d10 to your roll. You can do so after seeing the initial roll but before any of the roll's effects occur. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

features.name: Fiendish Resilience
features.body: Starting at 10th level, you can choose one damage type when you finish a short or long rest. You gain resistance to that damage type until you choose a different one with this feature. Damage from magical weapons or silver weapons ignores this resistance.

features.name: Hurl Through Hell
features.body: Starting at 14th level, when you hit a creature with an attack, you can use this feature to instantly transport the target through the lower planes. The creature disappears and hurtles through a nightmare landscape. At the end of your next turn, the target returns to the space it previously occupied, or the nearest unoccupied space. If the target is not a fiend, it takes 10d10 psychic damage as it reels from its horrific experience. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

subclasses.name: The Great Old One
subclasses.description: Your patron is a being of the Far Realm or an alien entity from the depths of space — Cthonic horrors whose alien minds touch yours across the gulfs between worlds. Hallmark: psionic-flavoured warlock with telepathy, mind-shielding, and a capstone that binds slain enemies as eternal thralls.

features.name: Expanded Spell List
features.body: The Great Old One lets you choose from an expanded list of spells when you learn a warlock spell. The following spells are added to the warlock spell list for you: 1st — Dissonant Whispers, Tasha's Hideous Laughter. 2nd — Detect Thoughts, Phantasmal Force. 3rd — Clairvoyance, Sending. 4th — Dominate Beast, Evard's Black Tentacles. 5th — Dominate Person, Telekinesis.

features.name: Awakened Mind
features.body: Starting at 1st level, your alien knowledge gives you the ability to touch the minds of other creatures. You can speak telepathically to any creature you can see within 30 feet of you. You don't need to share a language with the creature for it to understand your telepathic utterances, but the creature must be able to understand at least one language.

features.name: Entropic Ward
features.body: At 6th level, you learn to magically ward yourself against attack and to turn an enemy's failed strike into good luck for yourself. When a creature makes an attack roll against you, you can use your reaction to impose disadvantage on that roll. If the attack misses you, your next attack roll against the creature has advantage if you make it before the end of your next turn. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

features.name: Thought Shield
features.body: Starting at 10th level, your thoughts can't be read by telepathy or other means unless you allow it. You also have resistance to psychic damage, and whenever a creature deals psychic damage to you, that creature takes the same amount of damage that you do.

features.name: Create Thrall
features.body: At 14th level, you gain the ability to infect a humanoid's mind with the alien magic of your patron. You can use your action to touch an incapacitated humanoid. That creature is then charmed by you until a remove curse spell is cast on it, the charmed condition is removed from it, or you use this feature again. You can communicate telepathically with the charmed creature as long as the two of you are on the same plane of existence.

subclasses.name: The Hexblade
subclasses.description: Xanathar's most popular Warlock patron. You've made your pact with a mysterious entity from the Shadowfell — a force that manifests in sentient magic weapons. Hallmark: Hex Warrior turns your CHA into your weapon attack stat, making the Warlock the cleanest gish chassis in the game.

features.name: Expanded Spell List
features.body: The Hexblade lets you choose from an expanded list of spells when you learn a warlock spell. The following spells are added to the warlock spell list for you: 1st — Shield, Wrathful Smite. 2nd — Blur, Branding Smite. 3rd — Blink, Elemental Weapon. 4th — Phantasmal Killer, Staggering Smite. 5th — Banishing Smite, Cone of Cold.

features.name: Hexblade's Curse
features.body: Starting at 1st level, you gain the ability to place a baleful curse on someone. As a bonus action, choose one creature you can see within 30 feet of you. The target is cursed for 1 minute. The curse ends early if the target dies, you die, or you are incapacitated. Until the curse ends, you gain the following benefits: you gain a bonus to damage rolls against the cursed target equal to your proficiency bonus; any attack roll you make against the cursed target is a critical hit on a roll of 19 or 20; if the cursed target dies, you regain hit points equal to your warlock level + your Charisma modifier (minimum 1). Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

features.name: Hex Warrior
features.body: At 1st level, you acquire the training necessary to effectively arm yourself for battle. You gain proficiency with medium armor, shields, and martial weapons. The influence of your patron also allows you to mystically channel your will through a particular weapon. Whenever you finish a long rest, you can touch one weapon that you are proficient with and that lacks the two-handed property. When you attack with that weapon, you can use your Charisma modifier, instead of Strength or Dexterity, for the attack and damage rolls.

features.name: Accursed Specter
features.body: Starting at 6th level, you can curse the soul of a person you slay, temporarily binding it to your service. When you slay a humanoid, you can cause its spirit to rise from its corpse as a specter that fights for you. When the specter appears, it gains temporary hit points equal to half your warlock level. Roll initiative for the specter, which has its own turns. It remains in your service until the end of your next long rest, at which point it vanishes to the afterlife. Once you bind a specter with this feature, you can't use the feature again until you finish a long rest. (Specter is a companion — full companion mechanics land with step 18.)

features.name: Armor of Hexes
features.body: At 10th level, your hex grows more powerful. If the target cursed by your Hexblade's Curse hits you with an attack roll, you can use your reaction to roll a d6. On a 4 or higher, the attack instead misses you, regardless of its roll.

features.name: Master of Hexes
features.body: Starting at 14th level, you can spread your Hexblade's Curse from a slain creature to another creature. When the creature cursed by your Hexblade's Curse dies, you can apply the curse to a different creature you can see within 30 feet of you, provided you aren't incapacitated. When you apply the curse in this way, you don't regain hit points from the death of the previously cursed creature.
